options: The point-of-sale application captures each invoice at the counter and posts the daily sales summary to the ledger.
The payroll module computes the employer's provident fund contribution and passes the monthly accounting entry to the books.
The document management system stores scanned images of physical purchase invoices for seven years so that they can be retrieved on request.
The expense application authorises an employee claim against the limit configured for his grade before it is paid and accounted.
questions.explanation: The source creates an IT dependency when IT is used to initiate, authorise, record, process or report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements, and every element of that test must be satisfied. Storing scanned invoices supports retrieval only: the system neither initiates, authorises, records, processes nor reports financial data for inclusion in the financial statements, so no dependency arises. The other three satisfy the definition through recording, processing and authorising respectively. The decisive fact is the function performed on financial data destined for the financial statements, not the volume of financial content a system holds or the length of time it holds it.

questions.question: Assertion (A): An IT dependency arises where the fixed asset register module applies the straight-line formula to compute depreciation that is posted to the statement of profit and loss. Reason (R): IT is being used to process transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The source creates an IT dependency when IT is used to initiate, authorise, record, process or report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements. Depreciation computed by the module and posted to the profit or loss account is the system processing financial data for that inclusion, so the assertion is correct and the reason is the very condition that produces it, which disposes of the second alternative on the footing that the reason is not an unrelated true statement. The third alternative fails because the reason is a verbatim limb of the source's definition, and the fourth fails because the assertion follows directly from that same definition. The decisive limb of the definition here is processing, since neither a person nor another system performs the computation.

questions.question: In assessing reliance on IT, a statutory auditor examines a manufacturing entity's systems. Which situation falls within the source's definition of when an IT dependency is created?
options: The IT help desk logs and prioritises user complaints about slow screen response in the accounts module.
The production planning application schedules machine hours for internal capacity purposes and no output of the application enters the books of account.
Employees book leave in the human resource portal, which is not integrated with payroll or with the books of account.
The warehouse application records goods received notes which are used to recognise inventory and trade payables in the books.
questions.explanation: The definition turns on IT being used to initiate, authorise, record, process or report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements, and recording goods received notes that give rise to inventory and payable recognition is IT recording financial data for that inclusion. The first two situations involve support activity and operational scheduling with no financial data destined for the financial statements, and the leave portal fails because its data never reaches payroll or the books; if leave data fed payroll accounting the position would change. The decisive fact is whether the data handled by the system is intended for inclusion in the financial statements, not whether the data is commercial or financial in character.

questions.question: Which statement about the purposes served by identifying IT dependencies is INCORRECT?
options: It assists the auditor in identifying the extent of the entity's reliance upon IT in preparing the financial statements.
It substitutes for any assessment of whether the general IT controls implemented by management are operating effectively.
It assists in identifying the potential risks arising from the use of IT at the entity.
It enables the auditor to develop an audit approach that is both effective and efficient.
questions.explanation: The source lists three purposes of identifying IT dependencies, namely identifying the entity's reliance upon IT, identifying potential risks arising from the use of IT, and enabling the auditor to develop an effective and efficient audit approach, so the first, third and fourth statements are each supported. The second is not: the source confines identification to reliance, risk and approach, and nothing in it makes the identification of dependencies a substitute for assessing whether the general IT controls that management has implemented actually operate effectively, which is a separate matter. The decisive point is that identification is an enabling analytical step, not a conclusion on control performance. Candidates who read efficiency of approach as a licence to omit further work have over-read the third purpose.

questions.question:
Chirag Pharmaceuticals Limited operates on an ERP and has grown from 40 to 190 locations in two years. During planning of the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025, the engagement team identifies that IT is used to initiate, authorise, record, process and report transactions for inclusion in the financial statements. The team also identifies that the IT function holds privileged credentials capable of altering both configuration and posted data and that no procedure requires modifications to the ERP to be tracked and recorded. The engagement partner asks the team to first identify each point at which the ERP is relied upon for financial data and then to decide how much IT-specific audit effort is needed.

Which combination correctly represents the purposes that identifying IT dependencies serves under the source?
options: To identify the entity's reliance upon IT; to identify potential risks arising from the use of IT; to enable the auditor to develop an effective and efficient audit approach.
To identify the entity's reliance upon IT; to design specific general IT controls for each application; to identify potential risks arising from the use of IT.
To identify potential risks arising from the use of IT; to conclude on the operating effectiveness of automated controls; to enable the auditor to develop an effective and efficient audit approach.
To determine the scope of the internal audit function; to identify the entity's reliance upon IT; to conclude on the adequacy of management's documentation of its information system.
questions.explanation: The source states three purposes and the first alternative reproduces them, which matters most at Chirag because growth from 40 to 190 locations makes the extent of reliance on the ERP, rather than the number of staff, the driver of audit effort. The second alternative introduces the design of general IT controls, which the source treats as a management response to risks related to IT dependencies and not as a purpose of identifying them. The third introduces a conclusion on operating effectiveness, which follows from testing rather than from identification. The fourth substitutes internal audit scope and documentation adequacy, neither of which the source lists. The decisive discipline is that identification establishes reliance, points to risks and shapes the approach, and stops there.

questions.question:
Vardhman Synthetics Limited ("VSL") manufactures at three plants and maintains its books on a single ERP instance. During system implementation VSL's IT team copied the approval hierarchy of the prior standalone purchase module into the ERP, and the team retained its own emergency administrator credential, described internally as "break-fix access", which is not logged and is used at the IT team's discretion. Five IT arrangements are relevant to the audit of the financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025: (a) the ERP releases a purchase order only after the approving authority, fixed by value band in the workflow, has digitally approved it, and the order cannot be released without that approval; (b) the ERP applies the straight-line formula to the asset master, using cost and useful life captured at capitalisation, to compute monthly depreciation for posting to the statement of profit and loss; (c) VSL's treasury bank portal automatically pushes cleared daily transactions into the ERP cash ledger without any keying by VSL personnel; (d) the ERP generates an aged creditors report that the finance director reviews monthly before approving vendor statement reconciliations and that the audit team proposes to use for selecting confirmation balances; (e) the ERP permits a stores clerk to indenter a purchase order and, using the same user ID, to revise the delivery schedule of an order he himself had raised. VSL maintains a documented information security policy, and its annual access review is performed by the head of business operations but covers only 40 per cent of application users. VSL's change log shows that the ERP modification correcting a defective goods-reverse-capture screen was deployed directly by the IT team with no testing by any business user and with no entry in the change register, the entity having no procedure requiring that changes be tracked and recorded. Separately, the software vendor released a patch in October 2024 closing a critical vulnerability in the ERP, which VSL never deployed because no function owns the monitoring of vendor patch notifications. Data centre documentation at VSL covers physical entry, environmental controls and visitor registration.

Which classification of VSL's IT arrangements is correct under the source's five types of IT dependencies?
options: Arrangement (c) is a Report dependency and arrangement (b) is an Automated Control dependency.
Arrangement (c) is an Interface dependency and arrangement (b) is a Calculation dependency.
Arrangement (d) is a Calculation dependency and arrangement (a) is a Security dependency.
Arrangement (e) is an Automated Control dependency and arrangement (a) is an Interface dependency.
questions.explanation: The source defines interfaces as programmed logic that transfer data from one IT system to another, which is what the treasury portal to ERP push does, and calculations as accounting procedures performed by the IT system instead of a person, which is what the straight-line depreciation computation is. Arrangement (d) is a Report dependency because system generated reports are used in performance reviews, in selecting items for testing and in analytical procedures, so the third alternative misclassifies it, and arrangement (a) enforces a business rule through workflow, which makes it an Automated Control rather than a Security or Interface dependency. The first alternative misreads the bank push as a report, although nothing is generated for human use. The decisive discriminator is the destination of the output: a person using it makes it a Report, another system receiving it makes it an Interface.

questions.question:
Meridian Retail Limited ("MRL") operates 240 stores on a point-of-sale ("POS") application that posts daily sales summaries to a central finance system. Four facts emerge during the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025. (1) The finance team prepares the monthly gross-margin analytical review exclusively from the POS system-generated category-wise sales report. (2) The finance system applies the configured scheme to compute employee provident fund and depreciation for posting, instead of the accounting staff performing these computations. (3) A user audit performed by the IT support desk shows that the support team held administrator rights on both the POS and finance systems, and that no business management approval of such access had ever been obtained and no review had ever been performed outside the IT function. (4) Two months before the year end a power event at the hosted data centre made the previous nine days of posted transactions unavailable, and the entries had to be reconstructed from POS records. MRL maintains security policies and procedures and a change management policy, both current and reviewed annually; no change has been made to any of MRL's systems during the year and the change management policy has accordingly never been invoked. MRL has no procedure covering the backup of production systems and no test has ever been performed to establish whether data can be recovered.

Which pairing between a fact in MRL's environment and the type of IT dependency it creates is correct?
options: Fact (1) creates a Calculation dependency, because the gross margin percentage is a computed measure rather than a recorded amount.
Fact (3) creates an Automated Control dependency, because the administrator rights are configured within the systems themselves.
Fact (4) creates a Report dependency, because the nine days of unavailable data had to be reconstructed from POS records.
Fact (2) creates a Calculation dependency, because the accounting procedure is performed by the IT system instead of a person.
questions.explanation: The source defines calculations as accounting procedures performed by the IT system instead of a person, and provident fund and depreciation computed for posting fall squarely within it. Fact (1) is a Report dependency, since performance review is conducted from a system generated report and the fact that margin is expressed as a ratio does not convert the use of a report into a calculation dependency. Fact (3) concerns restriction of access and separation of roles, which the source places under Security, including segregation of duties, rather than under Automated Controls, which enforce business rules on transactions. Fact (4) evidences a failure of data availability and not a dependency type at all. The decisive test is what the source says the system does with the data, not the arithmetic content of the output.

questions.question: A housing finance entity's arrangements are set out below. Which one creates the dependency the source describes as programmed logic that transfers data from one IT system to another?
options: The loan origination module validates an applicant's income against the configured eligibility matrix before sanction is recorded.
The customer application generates a statement of account that the customer downloads and that the audit team inspects.
The core banking system transmits disbursal data captured at the branch to the general ledger module of the accounting application.
The interest engine computes accrual daily on outstanding principal and posts it to interest income.
questions.explanation: Transmission of disbursal data from core banking into the ledger module of a separate accounting application satisfies the definition of an Interface, because programmed logic moves data between IT systems and the transfer is itself the function performed. The eligibility check enforces a business rule and is an Automated Control; the statement of account is information generated by an IT system for use by persons, which is a Report; and the daily accrual is an accounting procedure performed by the system instead of a person, which is a Calculation. The decisive fact is that the data leaves one system for another instead of being consumed by a user as information or being computed within one system.

questions.question: The auditor of an e-commerce entity notes that its order application produces a category-wise return-rate report which the audit team proposes to treat as a dependency. On the source, which use of such a system generated report is contemplated?
options: Proving that the report was generated by a user whose access to the system was authorised.
Performing analytical procedures, selecting items for testing and use in performance reviews.
Replacing the substantive procedures the auditor would otherwise perform over the underlying transactions.
Establishing that the entity's automated controls operated effectively throughout the period.
questions.explanation: The source states that system generated reports are information generated by IT systems and that such reports are used in performance reviews, in selecting items for testing and in performing analytical procedures, and the second alternative reproduces those uses. The first attributes to a report an assurance about who generated it, which is a question of Access Security and of authorised data access rather than one of the uses the source lists. The third treats a report as evidence that displaces procedures over the underlying data, whereas the source treats it as information from which the auditor or management then works. The fourth attaches an assurance outcome to a report that the source assigns to no dependency type. The decisive limitation is that the source describes what reports are used for, not what they prove.

questions.question:
Which of the following represents the correct matching between the five types of IT dependencies in Column I and the arrangements described in Column II?

Column I: A. Automated Controls | B. Reports | C. Calculations | D. Security | E. Interfaces

Column II:
1. The asset module applies the straight-line formula configured at capitalisation to compute the monthly depreciation charge posted to the statement of profit and loss.
2. A purchase order cannot be released to the vendor unless the approving authority configured for that value band has digitally approved it in the workflow.
3. The application confines the ability to release a refund to users holding a different role from those who raise a credit note.
4. The aged debtors statement produced by the ledger is used by the finance director in the monthly collection review and by the audit team in selecting confirmation balances.
5. Attendance data captured at the gate is transferred nightly by programmed logic into the payroll module of the accounting application.
questions.explanation: Item 1 is an accounting procedure performed by the IT system instead of a person, so it is a Calculation and C-1; item 2 is designed into the environment to enforce a business rule, so it is an Automated Control and A-2; item 3 uses IT to determine separation of roles and responsibilities, so it falls under Security, including segregation of duties, and D-3; item 4 is information generated by an IT system used in a performance review and in selecting items for testing, so it is a Report and B-4; and item 5 is programmed logic transferring data from one IT system to another, so it is an Interface and E-5. The second alternative treats the enforced approval as a Report and the aged debtors statement as an Automated Control, reversing a rule enforced on a transaction and an output meant for human use. The third treats the nightly attendance transfer as a Calculation and the depreciation as an Interface, and the last treats the approval workflow as an Interface, although nothing is transferred to another system. The decisive discriminator is the verb in each definition, namely enforce, compute, restrict roles, inform a person, or transfer.

questions.question:
Meridian Retail Limited ("MRL") operates 240 stores on a point-of-sale ("POS") application that posts daily sales summaries to a central finance system. Four facts emerge during the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025. (1) The finance team prepares the monthly gross-margin analytical review exclusively from the POS system-generated category-wise sales report. (2) The finance system applies the configured scheme to compute employee provident fund and depreciation for posting, instead of the accounting staff performing these computations. (3) A user audit performed by the IT support desk shows that the support team held administrator rights on both the POS and finance systems, and that no business management approval of such access had ever been obtained and no review had ever been performed outside the IT function. (4) Two months before the year end a power event at the hosted data centre made the previous nine days of posted transactions unavailable, and the entries had to be reconstructed from POS records. MRL maintains security policies and procedures and a change management policy, both current and reviewed annually; no change has been made to any of MRL's systems during the year and the change management policy has accordingly never been invoked. MRL has no procedure covering the backup of production systems and no test has ever been performed to establish whether data can be recovered.

Which combination of actions responds to a control gap that MRL's facts actually disclose, consistently with the control objectives and example controls the source sets out for the areas of general IT controls?

Action 1: Require that access requests to the POS and finance applications be properly authorised and reviewed by management, being an example control under the Access Security objective.
Action 2: Introduce a change management policy and procedures, being an example control under the Program Change objective.
Action 3: Establish procedures for the backup of production systems and verify that data is appropriately backed up and recoverable, addressing the Data Centre objective.
Action 4: Extend the annual review of the security policies and procedures and of the change management policy so that they cover all 240 locations.
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Action 1 responds to fact (3), where administrator rights over both systems were held by the support desk with no approval by business management and no review outside IT, and the source's example control under Access Security is precisely that access requests to applications are properly authorised and reviewed by management. Action 3 responds to the disclosed absence of any backup procedure or recoverability test, taken with the power event that made nine days of posted transactions unavailable, which is what the Data Centre objective addresses. Actions 2 and 4 respond to no disclosed gap, because MRL already maintains current security policies and procedures and a current change management policy and made no change to any system during the year, so introducing and extending policies that are already in place leaves the failing areas untouched. The decisive discipline is to match the failing control to the area and objective the source assigns to it rather than to recommend every available control.

questions.question:
Vardhman Synthetics Limited ("VSL") manufactures at three plants and maintains its books on a single ERP instance. During system implementation VSL's IT team copied the approval hierarchy of the prior standalone purchase module into the ERP, and the team retained its own emergency administrator credential, described internally as "break-fix access", which is not logged and is used at the IT team's discretion. Five IT arrangements are relevant to the audit of the financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025: (a) the ERP releases a purchase order only after the approving authority, fixed by value band in the workflow, has digitally approved it, and the order cannot be released without that approval; (b) the ERP applies the straight-line formula to the asset master, using cost and useful life captured at capitalisation, to compute monthly depreciation for posting to the statement of profit and loss; (c) VSL's treasury bank portal automatically pushes cleared daily transactions into the ERP cash ledger without any keying by VSL personnel; (d) the ERP generates an aged creditors report that the finance director reviews monthly before approving vendor statement reconciliations and that the audit team proposes to use for selecting confirmation balances; (e) the ERP permits a stores clerk to indenter a purchase order and, using the same user ID, to revise the delivery schedule of an order he himself had raised. VSL maintains a documented information security policy, and its annual access review is performed by the head of business operations but covers only 40 per cent of application users. VSL's change log shows that the ERP modification correcting a defective goods-reverse-capture screen was deployed directly by the IT team with no testing by any business user and with no entry in the change register, the entity having no procedure requiring that changes be tracked and recorded. Separately, the software vendor released a patch in October 2024 closing a critical vulnerability in the ERP, which VSL never deployed because no function owns the monitoring of vendor patch notifications. Data centre documentation at VSL covers physical entry, environmental controls and visitor registration.

Which of the following statements about VSL's environment are correct?

Statement 1: Arrangement (d) is a Report dependency, and the use the audit team proposes to make of the aged creditors report is among the uses of system generated reports that the source contemplates.
Statement 2: Arrangement (a) creates an Automated Control dependency, because the approval requirement is designed into the IT environment to enforce a business rule.
Statement 3: Arrangement (e) evidences separation of roles determined by the IT environment and is therefore a Security dependency operating as intended.
Statement 4: The deployment of the goods-reverse-capture modification without business testing and without any entry in the change register is a failure of the example control that changes be adequately tracked and recorded, which sits under the Program Change objective.
options: 1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are supported. The source treats system generated reports as information used in performance reviews, in selecting items for testing and in analytical procedures, and using the aged creditors report to select confirmation balances is selecting items for testing, while a workflow that prevents release of a purchase order without the configured approval is a rule enforced on a transaction and therefore an Automated Control. Statement 4 correctly locates adequate tracking and recording of changes under the Program Change objective, which is concerned with modified systems continuing to meet the stated objectives. Statement 3 fails, and with it every combination containing it: the same user ID may both indenter an order and revise the delivery schedule of his own order, so the IT environment determines no separation of roles and the Security dependency is absent rather than operating as intended. The decisive fact is that a Security dependency requires the system to restrict which role may act, which arrangement (e) does not do.

questions.question:
Daksh Infra Limited ("DIL") operates an ERP for construction contracts. In August 2024 DIL's IT department, while resolving a performance complaint, modified the logic that determines the work-in-progress cost pool; the modification was released to production on the same day with no testing by the contracts or finance function. In January 2025 the IT department granted an external consultant permanent access to the production contract cost tables so that a report could be prepared on one occasion. Neither event was reported to management as an IT matter. The statutory auditor of DIL identifies that the ERP is used to record and process contract cost data for inclusion in the financial statements and therefore intends to rely on general IT controls.

Which one of the following correctly identifies a general IT control area and its objective for one of the two events in DIL's environment?
options: The January 2025 consultant access engages the Data Centre objective, that production systems are backed up to meet the stated objectives.
The August 2024 modification engages the Access Security objective, that data access is authorised to meet the stated objectives.
The January 2025 consultant access engages the Program Change objective, that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives.
The August 2024 modification engages the Program Change objective, that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives.
questions.explanation: The source states the Program Change objective as ensuring that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives, and a modification to the logic that determines the work-in-progress cost pool, released without testing by the contracts or finance function, is precisely a change whose continued correctness nobody verified. The consultant's permanent access to production contract cost tables is a matter for Access Security, whose objective is that data access is authorised to meet the stated objectives, so the first and third alternatives attach the access event to the wrong areas. The second alternative files the modification under Access Security, whose objective concerns authorisation of access rather than the behaviour of a modified system. The decisive fact is that one event changed a system and the other granted access, and the source assigns each to a different control area.

questions.question: An auditor documents the following conclusions about general IT controls at a listed entity. Which conclusion is INCORRECT on the source's statement of control objectives?
options: Because a developer altered the interest computation logic of the loan application and released it without verification, the Program Change objective is at risk.
Because the entity's documented security policy has not been revised since implementation, the Program Change objective is at risk.
Because a payroll executive can view the bank account details of all employees although her role requires access to none, the Access Security objective is at risk.
Because a fire at the hosted data centre destroyed the production database, which existed nowhere else, the Data Centre objective is at risk.
questions.explanation: The Program Change objective is stated by the source as ensuring that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives, so an unrevised security policy document does not engage it; the source places the maintenance of security policies and procedures as a control under Access Security, which makes the second conclusion the incorrect one. The remaining conclusions each attach a fact to the objective the source actually assigns: an unverified change to system logic, data access that is not confined to what has been authorised, and a production system that was not recoverable. The decisive distinction is between an example control that belongs to one area and the objective of a different area, which is exactly where the second conclusion slips.

questions.question:
Bharat Toolworks Limited records revenue through its ERP and the audit team assesses reliance on IT. The following IT arrangements are noted: purchase orders are released only after workflow approval by the authority configured for the value band; inventory issued to production is valued by the moving average basis that the ERP computes on every transaction; data captured on the shop-floor scanning handhelds is transmitted to the ERP production ledger by programmed logic; a system-generated scrap trend report is used by the audit team to select stores items for physical verification and by management in performance reviews; and the ERP restricts the ability to pass a journal for the capital account group to two named users, both of whom report to the chief financial officer. The audit team is specifically examining the arrangement by which inventory issued to production is valued by the moving average basis that the ERP computes on every transaction.

Which of the following general IT controls is MOST appropriate to address the risk arising specifically from the arrangement that the audit team is examining?
options: Ensure that access requests to the revenue application are properly authorised by, and reviewed by management outside, the IT function.
Maintain and review security policies and procedures covering the roles permitted to pass journals for the capital account group.
Maintain a change management policy and procedures and ensure that changes to the inventory valuation logic are adequately tracked and recorded.
Establish procedures for the backup of production systems and verify that data is appropriately backed up and recoverable.
questions.explanation: The arrangement being examined is a Calculation dependency, an accounting procedure performed by the IT system instead of a person, and the risk that matters is that the valuation logic is altered so that the moving average computation no longer produces the intended result. The source's Program Change objective is to ensure that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives and its example controls are the maintenance of a change management policy and procedures and adequate tracking and recording of changes, which the third alternative supplies. The first and second alternatives address Access Security, which governs who may reach data rather than whether programmed logic still behaves correctly. The fourth addresses recoverability of production systems, a different failure mode. The decisive fact is that the exposure is to modification of programmed accounting logic.

questions.question: A compliance officer reports the following observations to the audit committee of a manufacturing entity. Which observation indicates a failure of the Program Change area of general IT controls as the source frames that area?
options: The inventory valuation routine was altered by a developer, the altered logic was deployed without any testing, and the deployment was never recorded.
The IT support team can extend its own storage quota and database permissions without any approval from outside the IT function.
The transaction database of the previous financial year cannot be retrieved after a disk failure at the hosting facility.
The security policy permits vendor employees to retain remote access for six months after their ERP engagement ends.
questions.explanation: The Program Change area is directed at ensuring that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives, and its example controls are a maintained change management policy and adequate tracking and recording of changes, both of which the first observation fails at once. The second observation is the possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access and belongs to Access Security. The third concerns whether production systems are backed up and recoverable, which is the Data Centre objective. The fourth concerns who is permitted to reach data, again Access Security. The decisive fact is the presence of a system modification whose consequences were neither verified nor recorded, as distinct from failures of access or recoverability.

questions.question:
Pallav Imports Limited uses a cloud order-management application. During the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025 the following facts are recorded. (1) The IT team applied a security patch that changed the freight accrual logic; the finance function was not consulted, no testing was performed, and the change was not recorded anywhere outside the IT function's own mailbox. (2) The same four IT support personnel hold administrator rights on the application, and no access request for their rights was approved by business management nor reviewed by anyone outside IT. (3) The monthly credit-note summary used by the audit team to select items for testing was produced by the IT support desk, which holds administrator rights, using a desktop extract tool rather than by the application itself. (4) A storage failure at the service provider destroyed two weeks of posted transaction data, which had never been backed up and could not be recovered. (5) The finance head reconciles the goods received not invoiced balance monthly by comparing the application's system-generated ageing report with the general ledger.

Which of the following pairings of the storage failure with a general IT control area and its stated objective is correct?
options: Program Change, to ensure modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives, because the destruction of data followed the security patch applied by the IT team.
Access Security, to ensure that data access is authorised to meet the stated objectives, because unrestricted administrator rights caused the loss.
Data Centre, to ensure production systems are backed up to meet the stated objectives, because the production data was neither backed up nor recoverable.
Data Centre, to ensure production systems are backed up to meet the stated objectives, because the freight accrual change was not recorded outside the IT function's mailbox.
questions.explanation: The source assigns to the Data Centre area the objective of ensuring that production systems are backed up to meet the stated objectives and supports it with the control that data is appropriately backed up and recoverable, which is exactly the failure described, so the third pairing is correct. The first two place the event under areas whose objectives do not concern recoverability, and nothing in the facts links the storage failure either to the applied patch or to the administrator rights. The fourth selects the right area and objective but the wrong reasoning, because the absence of a record of the freight accrual change is a Program Change matter and has no bearing on whether data could be restored. The decisive fact is that data became irrecoverable, not that the events preceding the loss were undocumented.

questions.question:
A statutory auditor records four stages in the order in which the source supports them occurring during the audit of an automated environment.

Stage 1: IT is used to initiate, authorise, record, process or report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements.
Stage 2: An IT dependency is created, and identifying it identifies the entity's reliance upon IT.
Stage 3: Potential risks arising from the use of IT are identified and the auditor develops an effective and efficient audit approach.
Stage 4: Management implements general IT controls to address the risks related to the IT dependencies.
Which of the following represents the correct sequence?
questions.explanation: The use of IT to handle financial data is the cause and the dependency the consequence, so stage 1 must precede stage 2, which disposes of the first alternative. Identifying IT dependencies is what enables the auditor to identify potential risks arising from the use of IT and to develop the audit approach, so stage 3 follows stage 2 rather than preceding it, disposing of the third and fourth alternatives. The management response is stated by the source as addressing risks related to IT dependencies, so it necessarily follows identification. The decisive link is that dependency identification sits between the existence of the arrangement and both the risk assessment and the control response.

questions.question: In the audit of a fully automated entity, the engagement team records four conclusions about the respective roles of management and the auditor. Which conclusion is correct on the source?
options: The auditor designs and implements general IT controls, and management identifies the IT dependencies on which those controls operate.
Management identifies the IT dependencies and implements automated controls to enforce business rules, after which the auditor assesses the audit approach.
The auditor's identification of IT dependencies determines the general IT controls that management is required to implement in each application area.
The auditor identifies the IT dependencies and the risks arising from the use of IT, and management may implement general IT controls to address the risks related to those dependencies.
questions.explanation: The source assigns identification of IT dependencies to the auditor, since it helps to identify reliance on IT, to identify potential risks arising from the use of IT and to develop an effective and efficient audit approach, and it assigns the implementation of general IT controls to management, so the fourth conclusion is correct. The first reverses both roles, and the second makes dependency identification a management act while also making the audit approach consequential on management's controls. The third fails on two counts, because it treats the management response as mandatory although the source says management may implement such controls, and it treats identification by the auditor as determining what management must do. The decisive facts are who identifies and who implements, and the permissive framing of the latter.

questions.question: In an integrated audit of an insurance entity, the audit team records four findings. Which finding is correctly matched both to the type of IT dependency involved and to the general IT control area that must be effective for that dependency to remain reliable?
options: A claims module that approves settlement only within configured limits is an Automated Control dependency whose reliability depends principally on the Data Centre objective.
An interface feeding policy data from the underwriting portal to the ledger is an Interface dependency whose reliability depends on the Access Security objective alone.
A system-generated claims ageing report used by management in monthly reviews is a Report dependency whose reliability depends on the Program Change objective and nothing else.

An actuarial module computing incurred-but-not-reported claims is a Calculation dependency whose reliability depends on the Program Change objective, since a change to the computation would defeat it.
questions.explanation: The second and third alternatives are unsound because of the exclusions they assert: an interface is exposed to changes in the transfer logic and to loss of the data moved, so confining its reliability to Access Security alone is wrong, and a report used in reviews is exposed to changes in report configuration as well as to access and recoverability, so the assertion that it depends on one objective and nothing else cannot be supported. The first alternative correctly names an Automated Control dependency, since the module enforces a business rule, but attaches it to the Data Centre objective, which concerns backup of production systems, whereas the exposure of a business rule is to the rule being changed, which is Program Change. The fourth alternative is sound on both limbs, because computing an accounting amount instead of a person is the source's definition of a Calculation and the objective that modified systems continue to meet the stated objectives is the protection such a dependency needs. The decisive requirement is that both halves of the answer be correct.

questions.question:
Anand Handloom Limited maintains its books on a single ERP. The ERP releases a purchase order only after approval by the authority configured in the workflow for the value band, computes depreciation on the straight-line formula configured in the asset master, transfers data captured at the weavers' service centres into the ERP through programmed logic, produces a system-generated aged debtors report that the audit team uses to select items for testing, and restricts the roles that may create a vendor and release payment to different user groups. The IT team holds an unlogged "platform owner" credential for use during server maintenance and has the ability to change configuration and posted transaction data. The audit team is also told that the security patch closing a critical vulnerability in the ERP, released by the software vendor in October 2024, was never applied because no one in the IT function owned the responsibility for monitoring vendor patch notifications. The IT department further has no procedure requiring that modifications to the ERP be tracked and recorded.

Which of the following statements about Anand's environment are correct?

Statement 1: IT is used to initiate, authorise, record, process and report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements, and IT dependencies are therefore created.
Statement 2: The unlogged platform owner credential evidences the risk of the possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access, and the unapplied October 2024 patch evidences the risk of failure to make necessary update to IT applications or other aspects of the IT environment.
Statement 3: The absence of a procedure requiring that modifications be tracked and recorded is a failure of an example control under the Program Change objective, while the ability of the IT function to alter posted data is addressed by the Access Security objective that data access is authorised to meet the stated objectives.
Statement 4: Because the ERP restricts vendor creation and payment release to different user groups, Anand has no exposure to the risk of unauthorised changes to data, that risk being fully answered by the configured segregation.
options: 1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are each supported: statement 1 applies the definition of when dependencies arise to the arrangements described, statement 2 pairs two facts with two separately listed risks, and statement 3 places change tracking under Program Change and unauthorised data alteration under Access Security, which are the areas the source assigns them to. Statement 4 fails, and therefore every combination containing it fails, because the separation of vendor creation from payment release is itself a Security dependency, namely segregation of duties enabled by the IT environment, and its presence does not remove exposure to unauthorised changes to data while an unlogged platform owner credential allows the IT function to alter posted data. The decisive fact is that a control that depends on IT cannot answer a risk arising from IT unless the supporting general IT controls operate.

questions.question:
Bharat Toolworks Limited records revenue through its ERP and the audit team assesses reliance on IT. The following IT arrangements are noted: purchase orders are released only after workflow approval by the authority configured for the value band; inventory issued to production is valued by the moving average basis that the ERP computes on every transaction; data captured on the shop-floor scanning handhelds is transmitted to the ERP production ledger by programmed logic; a system-generated scrap trend report is used by the audit team to select stores items for physical verification and by management in performance reviews; and the ERP restricts the ability to pass a journal for the capital account group to two named users, both of whom report to the chief financial officer. The audit team is specifically examining the arrangement by which inventory issued to production is valued by the moving average basis that the ERP computes on every transaction.

Which of the following statements about the dependencies created by Bharat's arrangements are correct?

Statement 1: Restricting the ability to pass a journal for the capital account group to two named users creates a Security dependency, because the IT environment restricts access to information and determines separation of roles and responsibilities.
Statement 2: Valuing inventory issued to production at the moving average basis computed by the ERP on every transaction creates an Automated Control dependency, because the valuation is enforced by the system.
Statement 3: Transmitting shop-floor scanning data to the ERP production ledger by programmed logic creates an Interface dependency.
Statement 4: Using the system-generated scrap trend report to select stores items for physical verification creates a Report dependency.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect and every combination containing it therefore fails, because a system that computes an accounting measure instead of a person creates a Calculation dependency, whereas Automated Controls are designed to enforce business rules such as the approval requirement in Bharat's purchase order workflow. Statement 1 is correct because the source expressly places segregation of duties within the Security type as the arrangement by which IT restricts access to information and determines separation of roles and responsibilities. Statements 3 and 4 are correct because programmed logic transferring data between systems is an Interface and a report used in selecting items for testing is information generated by an IT system used for a review or test purpose. The decisive discriminator between statements 1 and 2 is whether the system performs a computation or confines who may act.

questions.category: Risks arising from use of IT
questions.question:
Suraksha Textiles Limited uses an ERP in which three matters come to the auditor's attention during the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025. First, the ERP workflow blocks release of a purchase order above Rs 5 lakh unless an additional digital approval of the chief operating officer is captured. Second, a shared "operations support" user ID, known to be used by three accounts executives, was used to alter the payment terms of 18 vendors during the year, and the IT department's own access register had granted that user ID the ability to modify the vendor master because the ticket raising the request came from accounts. Third, the ERP produced a credit-note ageing report used by the commercial director in monthly performance reviews and by the audit team to select items for testing, but the report was run only once, in April 2024, and was not regenerated for the remaining period.

Which of the following statements about Suraksha's environment are correct?

Statement 1: The IT department's grant of vendor master modification rights to a shared user ID, on the strength of a ticket from accounts and without management authorisation or review, evidences the risk of the possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access.
Statement 2: The alteration of the payment terms of 18 vendors through that shared ID evidences the risk of unauthorised access to data or improper changes to data.
Statement 3: Reliance on a credit-note ageing report generated once in April 2024 evidences the risk of inappropriate manual intervention.
Statement 4: The ERP block that prevents release of a purchase order above Rs 5 lakh without additional approval creates a Security dependency.
options: 1 and 4 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 identify two distinct risks that the source lists separately: the extension of privileged modification rights arranged without management authorisation is the possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access, and the alterations made through the shared ID are improper changes to data. Statement 3 fails because a report that has simply not been regenerated discloses reliance on outdated system information, whereas inappropriate manual intervention concerns a person interfering with a process the IT environment performs. Statement 4 fails because a workflow block that prevents release of an order without approval enforces a business rule and therefore creates an Automated Control dependency, while the Security type concerns restricting access to information and separating roles. The decisive point in statement 4 is that the constraint operates on the transaction, not on the identity of the person operating.

questions.question:
Nirman Estates Limited operates on a single ERP instance. During the pre-audit walkthrough the audit team records the following facts: (i) the ERP releases a purchase order only after approval by the authority configured in the workflow for that value band; (ii) an interface feeds property application data captured by the sales team into the revenue module; (iii) the ERP computes depreciation on completed inventory blocks using the formula configured in the asset master; (iv) a system-generated pending-sales-listing report is used by the audit team to select property-wise balance confirmations and by management in monthly performance reviews; (v) the ERP restricts the users who may record a refund and the users who may release the payment of that refund to different role groups. The IT department confirms that no configuration change of any kind has been made to the ERP since go-live, because all change requests were rejected by the change management committee on cost grounds.

Which of the following statements correctly analyses Nirman's environment?
options: The use of the pending sales listing report in management's monthly performance review and by the audit team in selecting confirmations evidences the risk of data loss or data corruption.
The interface feeding property application data into the revenue module creates an Automated Control dependency, because it enforces the transfer of that data.
The absence of any configuration change since go-live means that the risk of unauthorised changes to IT applications or other aspects of the IT environment need not be considered at Nirman.
The restriction of refund recording and refund payment release to different role groups creates a Security dependency, because IT restricts access to information and determines separation of roles.
questions.explanation: The source places security including segregation of duties within the IT dependency types as being enabled by the IT environment to restrict access to information and to determine separation of roles and responsibilities, and a refund recording and payment release split between role groups is that arrangement. The first alternative attaches a risk to the ordinary use of a system generated report, which is a Report dependency and not evidence of loss or corruption. The second misclassifies programmed transfer logic as an Automated Control, although nothing is enforced on a transaction. The third fails because the listed risk is an exposure to unauthorised change and does not cease merely because no change has yet occurred, so the position would change only if the auditor treated the risk as one that had already materialised rather than one that may. The decisive fact is what the arrangement does, namely separating roles, rather than the monetary amount involved.

questions.question: A logistics entity maintains two applications. Its shipping application records goods received notes, which are used to recognise inventory and trade payables in the books. Its quality module records test-pass certificates for the inspectors' internal use only, and no output of that module reaches the books of account. The auditor concludes today that an IT dependency exists in respect of the shipping application and no IT dependency exists in respect of the quality module. Which single change to these facts would alter that conclusion?
options: No invoice may be posted unless the quality module has first recorded a pass certificate for the consignment, so that revenue recognition waits on that entry.
The IT team applies a performance patch to the quality module, following which certificates are recorded within seconds instead of several minutes.
The quality module is migrated from the entity's own server to a server hosted and administered by a third-party provider.
The quality module begins sending automatic reminders to inspectors whose pending certificates are more than two days old.
questions.explanation: The conclusion changes only if the quality module starts being used to initiate, authorise, record, process or report transactions or other financial data for inclusion in the financial statements, and making revenue recognition conditional on a pass certificate places the module in the authorise and record limbs of that definition. Faster response after a patch (second alternative) changes service quality, not the function performed on financial data, and a change of hosting arrangements (third alternative) is irrelevant, because the definition is indifferent to where the application runs. Automatic reminders to inspectors (fourth alternative) concern the workflow of a non-financial module and no financial data destined for the financial statements. The decisive fact is the destination and function of the data, not the location of the server or the speed of the application.

questions.question:
Pallav Imports Limited uses a cloud order-management application. During the audit of the year ended 31 March 2025 the following facts are recorded. (1) The IT team applied a security patch that changed the freight accrual logic; the finance function was not consulted, no testing was performed, and the change was not recorded anywhere outside the IT function's own mailbox. (2) The same four IT support personnel hold administrator rights on the application, and no access request for their rights was approved by business management nor reviewed by anyone outside IT. (3) The monthly credit-note summary used by the audit team to select items for testing was produced by the IT support desk, which holds administrator rights, using a desktop extract tool rather than by the application itself. (4) A storage failure at the service provider destroyed two weeks of posted transaction data, which had never been backed up and could not be recovered. (5) The finance head reconciles the goods received not invoiced balance monthly by comparing the application's system-generated ageing report with the general ledger.

Which of the following statements about Pallav's environment are correct?

Statement 1: The freight accrual change made without consultation or testing and recorded nowhere outside the IT function's own mailbox evidences a failure of the example controls stated for the Program Change area.
Statement 2: The credit-note summary the audit team uses to select items for testing is not a system generated report within the source's meaning, because it was produced by administrators using a desktop extract tool rather than by the application.
Statement 3: Permanent administrator rights held by four support personnel without business approval or review engage the Access Security objective and its example control that access requests be properly authorised and reviewed by management.
Statement 4: The absence of any backup procedure for posted transaction data engages the Access Security objective, because the storage failure was the consequence of unrestricted administrator rights.
options: 1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are each correct. The Program Change area is supported by the example controls that a change management policy and procedures are maintained and that changes are adequately tracked and recorded, and the freight accrual change failed both, since no policy governed it and no record of it exists outside IT's mailbox. The source defines reports as information generated by IT systems, so a manual desktop extract produced by privileged users is not a system generated report and cannot be relied on as a Report dependency in the same way, although it does bear on Access Security. Statement 4 is incorrect: unrecoverable data engages the Data Centre objective, that production systems are backed up to meet the stated objectives, and nothing in the facts attributes the storage failure to the administrator rights. The decisive discipline is that a gap belongs to the objective the source states for it and not to the area that shares its symptom.

questions.question:
Case: Kaveri Logistics Ltd is a listed freight-forwarding company whose audit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is being conducted by M/s Suresh Menon & Co. During the audit the team is informed of five separate IT incidents reported in the period.
(a) Files on the finance team's shared drive became unreadable, and a note on every screen demanded payment in cryptocurrency, stating that a decryption key would be released only on payment. No file had been copied outside the network and nothing had been deleted.
(b) Payroll staff had installed a no-cost invoice-format converter downloaded from a website; the converter performed the conversion but had also opened a remote-access channel on the workstation.
(c) The security operations centre established that no file had been written to disk during a third intrusion; the intruder had run commands using the scripting utility supplied as part of the server operating system.
(d) Warehouse staff received text messages, appearing to come from a well-known courier company, asking them to share their OTP and personal details to release a consignment.
(e) The chief executive officer's assistant received a telephone call, and later a voice message, from a person claiming to be the relationship manager of the company's bank, seeking the assistant's login details.

Which one of the following combinations correctly classifies incidents (a), (b) and (c) under the four subsets of malware given in the source?
options: (a) Denial-of-Service attack; (b) Mobile malware; (c) Trojan
(a) Ransomware; (b) Trojan; (c) Fileless malware
(a) Ransomware; (b) Fileless malware; (c) Trojan
(a) Email spoofing; (b) Trojan; (c) Fileless malware
questions.explanation: Ransomware is described as the adversary encrypting the victim's data and offering the decryption key in exchange for payment, which is exactly what (a) records; the absence of copying or deletion does not disturb that description, since encryption plus a payment-for-key offer is its whole substance. A Trojan is malware which appears to be legitimate software disguised as a harmless file such as a free download, and the no-cost converter in (b) performed the conversion advertised while carrying the malicious remote-access channel, so the disguise is the decisive fact. Fileless malware is malicious activity which uses legitimate tools built into the system to execute a cyber-attack, and (c) states that nothing was written to disk and the operating system's own scripting utility was used. The combination which reverses (b) and (c) is the trap: a converter that arrives as a downloaded file is not "fileless", and a tool already inside the server is not a disguised download. Retaining a Denial-of-Service label for (a) fails because no flood of false requests is alleged, and mobile malware is inapplicable to (c) because no mobile device was targeted; treating (a) as email spoofing fails because no email with a forged sender address is involved.

questions.question:
Case: Kaveri Logistics Ltd is a listed freight-forwarding company whose audit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is being conducted by M/s Suresh Menon & Co. During the audit the team is informed of five separate IT incidents reported in the period.
(a) Files on the finance team's shared drive became unreadable, and a note on every screen demanded payment in cryptocurrency, stating that a decryption key would be released only on payment. No file had been copied outside the network and nothing had been deleted.
(b) Payroll staff had installed a no-cost invoice-format converter downloaded from a website; the converter performed the conversion but had also opened a remote-access channel on the workstation.
(c) The security operations centre established that no file had been written to disk during a third intrusion; the intruder had run commands using the scripting utility supplied as part of the server operating system.
(d) Warehouse staff received text messages, appearing to come from a well-known courier company, asking them to share their OTP and personal details to release a consignment.
(e) The chief executive officer's assistant received a telephone call, and later a voice message, from a person claiming to be the relationship manager of the company's bank, seeking the assistant's login details.

Compare incidents (d) and (e). Which analysis of the two is correct, and identifies the decisive difference between them?
options: Both incidents are whaling, because the source treats any phishing incident which results in the disclosure of login or personal information as whaling.
Incident (d) is smishing and incident (e) is whaling, because a call placed to the chief executive officer's assistant is an attack on a senior employee.
Incident (d) is smishing and incident (e) is vishing; the decisive difference is the channel, text messages in (d) and calls and voice messages in (e).
Neither incident is phishing, because the source confines phishing to enticing a victim to download a malicious file which installs viruses.
questions.explanation: Phishing is described as using email, SMS, phone and social media to entice a victim to share sensitive information such as passwords or to download a malicious file, so drawing out an OTP and login details without any download is squarely within it, and the analysis which denies this for want of a download is wrong. Smishing is the fraudulent practice of sending text messages pretending from reputable companies to induce individuals to reveal personal information, which matches (d); vishing, or voice phishing, is the fraudulent use of calls and voice messages pretending from reputable companies to convince individuals to reveal private information, which matches (e). The element which separates those two sub-types in the source is the channel, not the identity of the victim and not the subject matter of the message. Whaling is the variant defined by targeting senior employees to steal money or information; in (e) the victim is the chief executive officer's assistant rather than a senior employee, so the seniority element is missing and neither analysis resting on whaling can be sustained.

questions.question:
Case: Kaveri Logistics Ltd is a listed freight-forwarding company whose audit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is being conducted by M/s Suresh Menon & Co. During the audit the team is informed of five separate IT incidents reported in the period.
(a) Files on the finance team's shared drive became unreadable, and a note on every screen demanded payment in cryptocurrency, stating that a decryption key would be released only on payment. No file had been copied outside the network and nothing had been deleted.
(b) Payroll staff had installed a no-cost invoice-format converter downloaded from a website; the converter performed the conversion but had also opened a remote-access channel on the workstation.
(c) The security operations centre established that no file had been written to disk during a third intrusion; the intruder had run commands using the scripting utility supplied as part of the server operating system.
(d) Warehouse staff received text messages, appearing to come from a well-known courier company, asking them to share their OTP and personal details to release a consignment.
(e) The chief executive officer's assistant received a telephone call, and later a voice message, from a person claiming to be the relationship manager of the company's bank, seeking the assistant's login details.

Attention is on incident (c). What changes if the facts of (c) are modified so that the intruder instead deposited on the server a disguised no-cost utility, obtained by the accounts staff as a free download, which they themselves executed?
options: Nothing changes: the intrusion would remain fileless malware, because the server is a legitimate system, every attack must execute through some tool already present on the system it attacks, and the utility here came with the operating system.
The classification would move to ransomware, because a utility obtained free of charge always carries an implied demand for value in return for its use.
The classification would move to spear phishing, because a free download is obtained only by enticing a person to act on the message which offers it.

The classification would move from fileless malware to Trojan, the decisive fact being that the code would no longer run through tools built into the system but would itself be software disguised as a harmless free download.
questions.explanation: The source defines fileless malware by its mechanism, namely malicious activity which uses legitimate tools built into the system to execute a cyber-attack, and defines a Trojan as malware which appears to be legitimate software disguised as harmless files like free downloads. Replace the built-in scripting utility with a downloaded disguised program and the fact that supported the fileless label disappears while the description of a Trojan is satisfied word for word, so the reclassification turns entirely on how the malicious code reached and ran on the server. Retaining the fileless label ignores that a file was in fact deposited, which is the opposite of the description. Moving to ransomware is unsupportable because that description requires the adversary to encrypt the victim's data and to offer the decryption key in exchange for payment, neither of which is alleged. The spear-phishing answer is the most attractive alternative, because phishing does extend to enticing a victim to download a malicious file and the download here was induced; but the question asks what changes within the malware subsets, and among those subsets the disguised free download is the very feature which distinguishes a Trojan.

questions.category: Cyber Risks – Cyber-attack: meaning and intents
questions.question:
Case: Kaveri Logistics Ltd is a listed freight-forwarding company whose audit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is being conducted by M/s Suresh Menon & Co. During the audit the team is informed of five separate IT incidents reported in the period.
(a) Files on the finance team's shared drive became unreadable, and a note on every screen demanded payment in cryptocurrency, stating that a decryption key would be released only on payment. No file had been copied outside the network and nothing had been deleted.
(b) Payroll staff had installed a no-cost invoice-format converter downloaded from a website; the converter performed the conversion but had also opened a remote-access channel on the workstation.
(c) The security operations centre established that no file had been written to disk during a third intrusion; the intruder had run commands using the scripting utility supplied as part of the server operating system.
(d) Warehouse staff received text messages, appearing to come from a well-known courier company, asking them to share their OTP and personal details to release a consignment.
(e) The chief executive officer's assistant received a telephone call, and later a voice message, from a person claiming to be the relationship manager of the company's bank, seeking the assistant's login details.

Based on the case, which of the following statements are correct when the incidents are tested against the source's definition of a cyber-attack?
Statement 1: Incident (a) is within the definition, because the enumerated intents include altering and disabling data, so the absence of theft or deletion does not take it outside.
Statement 2: Incident (b) is outside the definition, because the converter genuinely performed the conversion for which it was downloaded and therefore did nothing to the data.
Statement 3: Incident (d) is within the definition, because enticement to share sensitive information such as passwords is an attempt to gain unauthorized access to a computing system or network.
Statement 4: Incident (c) is outside the definition, because tools supplied with the operating system cannot form part of an attempt to gain unauthorized access.
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: A cyber-attack is an attempt to gain unauthorized access to a computing system or network with intent to damage, steal, expose, alter, disable or destroy data; the intents are stated in the alternative, so rendering the finance data unreadable and unusable satisfies them and statement 1 is correct. Statement 3 is correct, since phishing through SMS to obtain an OTP and personal details is an attempt to gain unauthorized access through the human user. Statement 2 is wrong because the converter opened a remote-access channel, which is unauthorized access, and malware is defined by a program or code created with intent to do harm to a computer, network or server rather than by whether its cover function also worked. Statement 4 is wrong because fileless malware is expressly described as malicious activity which uses legitimate tools built into the system to execute a cyber-attack, so the legitimate origin of the utility does not place incident (c) outside the definition; every combination which admits statement 2 or statement 4, and the combination which omits statement 3, therefore fails.

questions.question:
Case: During the audit of Aashirvad Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026, four separate deceptions were reported to the audit team.
(i) An email addressed to the chief financial officer, showing the chairperson's own address as its sender, instructed the immediate release of an advance to a "priority vendor"; the sender address had in fact been fabricated.
(ii) A supplier, asked to verify an invoice, typed its username and password into a login page at an address which imitated the company's supplier portal but was not the company's domain.
(iii) A finance executive received an email naming him personally and referring to the travel dates in his approved leave record, asking him to open the attached "revised itinerary", which installed a virus on his laptop.
(iv) A storekeeper received a telephone call from a person claiming to be from a reputed insurance company and, being told that his claim would otherwise lapse, disclosed his bank account details.

Match each concept in Column I with the incident in Column II to which the source's description fits MOST specifically.
Column I: A. Whaling  B. Domain spoofing  C. Spear phishing  D. Vishing
Column II: 1. Incident (i)  2. Incident (ii)  3. Incident (iii)  4. Incident (iv)
Which of the following represents the correct matching?
questions.explanation: Whaling is the social-engineering attack specifically targeting senior employees with the purpose of stealing money or information, and (i) is addressed to the chief financial officer to extract an advance, so A-1. Domain spoofing is described as a form of phishing in which the attacker impersonates a known business with a fake website or domain to be trusted, which is the imitation supplier portal in (ii), so B-2. Spear phishing targets specific individuals or organizations typically through malicious emails, and (iii) names the finance executive personally and uses his leave record to sell the attachment, so C-3. Vishing is the fraudulent use of calls and voice messages pretending from reputable companies to convince individuals to reveal private information, matching the insurance-company call in (iv), so D-4. The matching which exchanges A and C is the principal trap: it treats the personally targeted executive as the senior victim and the chief financial officer as merely a targeted individual, whereas it is the seniority of the target, not the personalisation of the message, which separates whaling from spear phishing, and (iii) does not describe a senior employee at all.

questions.question:
Case: During the audit of Aashirvad Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026, four separate deceptions were reported to the audit team.
(i) An email addressed to the chief financial officer, showing the chairperson's own address as its sender, instructed the immediate release of an advance to a "priority vendor"; the sender address had in fact been fabricated.
(ii) A supplier, asked to verify an invoice, typed its username and password into a login page at an address which imitated the company's supplier portal but was not the company's domain.
(iii) A finance executive received an email naming him personally and referring to the travel dates in his approved leave record, asking him to open the attached "revised itinerary", which installed a virus on his laptop.
(iv) A storekeeper received a telephone call from a person claiming to be from a reputed insurance company and, being told that his claim would otherwise lapse, disclosed his bank account details.

Which of the following statements are correct in the light of the source's classifications?
Statement 1: Incident (i) answers to two descriptions at once - email spoofing, being an attack which targets a business by using emails with forged sender addresses, and whaling, because it targets a senior employee to obtain money.
Statement 2: Incident (ii) is treated by the source as a form of phishing even though it is listed as a type of spoofing.
Statement 3: Incident (iii) cannot be phishing, because the source confines phishing to enticing a victim to share sensitive information such as passwords.
Statement 4: Incident (iv) would cease to be vishing if the caller had asked the storekeeper to reveal private information rather than money, since vishing is described as obtaining money.
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: The source's categories overlap by design. Domain spoofing is listed among the types of spoofing yet is defined as a form of phishing, which makes statement 2 correct, and the forged sender address in (i) combined with a senior-employee target for money satisfies both the email-spoofing and the whaling descriptions, which makes statement 1 correct. Statement 3 is wrong because phishing is defined as using email, SMS, phone and social media to entice a victim either to share sensitive information or to download a malicious file that will install viruses on the computer or phone, and (iii) is the download limb; it also answers to the spear-phishing sub-type, so the parent description is not excluded. Statement 4 is wrong because vishing is described as convincing individuals to reveal private information, not money, and the storekeeper's disclosure of bank details is exactly that. The two combinations which admit statement 3, and the combination which admits statement 4, therefore fail.

questions.question:
Case: During the audit of Aashirvad Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026, four separate deceptions were reported to the audit team.
(i) An email addressed to the chief financial officer, showing the chairperson's own address as its sender, instructed the immediate release of an advance to a "priority vendor"; the sender address had in fact been fabricated.
(ii) A supplier, asked to verify an invoice, typed its username and password into a login page at an address which imitated the company's supplier portal but was not the company's domain.
(iii) A finance executive received an email naming him personally and referring to the travel dates in his approved leave record, asking him to open the attached "revised itinerary", which installed a virus on his laptop.
