Senior associate Neha proposes Power BI for need (i) because Power BI can aggregate and analyse data, and ACL for need (iv) because ACL is the best-known audit software in the industry.
Which of the above statements are INCORRECT?
Statement 1: Neha's proposal of Power BI for need (i) is not supportable, because the material describes Power BI as a platform for aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data for non-technical business users and as a reporting tool in an interactive dashboard to higher management, not as fraud detection and prevention software.
Statement 2: Neha's proposal of ACL for need (iv) is not supportable, because the material attributes the quick, accurate and consistent conduct of audit and assurance engagements, the streamlining of processes and the elimination of routine tasks to CaseWare.
Statement 3: If need (ii) were dropped from the case, Alteryx would have no described application left, because the material limits Alteryx to consolidating financial or operational data to assess controls.
Statement 4: Need (iii) is properly met by CaseWare, because sharing analytical insights is the function the material treats as distinctive to CaseWare.
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct readings of the material and therefore are not answers to a question asking for the incorrect statements: the material ties fraud detection and prevention to ACL Analytics and the conduct of engagements with routine tasks eliminated to CaseWare. Statement 3 is incorrect because the material gives Alteryx two described functions - consolidating financial or operational data to assess controls and automating set procedures performed periodically such as reconciliations, consolidations, system integrations and continuous audits - so dropping need (ii) would not exhaust its stated applications; the decisive fact is that the material expressly extends Alteryx beyond consolidation. Statement 4 is also incorrect: although CaseWare shares analytical insights, the interactive dashboard for reporting to higher management and the reference to non-technical business users appear only in the Power BI description, which is what need (iii) calls for. Any option that includes statements 1 or 2 fails, because those two are correct, and the all-inclusive option fails for the same reason.

questions.question:
Indira Textiles Ltd. is a power-loom weaving unit running fourteen ERP modules. During the FY 2025-26 audit, engagement partner R. Venkatesh asks his team to meet four separate needs.
Need (i): the accounts payable ledger of 6.4 lakh invoice lines must be examined for irregularities indicating fictitious vendors, and the tool selected must be one which the study material describes as a data extraction and analysis software used for fraud detection and prevention.
Need (ii): the monthly bank, inter-company and GST reconciliations, the quarterly consolidation, two system integrations and a continuous audit routine, all being set procedures performed periodically, must be carried out without repeat manual effort.
Need (iii): the audit committee, consisting mainly of non-technical independent directors, wants the findings aggregated, analysed, visualised and shared through an interactive dashboard for reporting to higher management.
Need (iv): the firm runs a standardised audit file across thirty concurrent engagements and wants to conduct these audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently, streamlining processes and eliminating routine tasks while sharing analytical insights.
Senior associate Neha proposes Power BI for need (i) because Power BI can aggregate and analyse data, and ACL for need (iv) because ACL is the best-known audit software in the industry.
Suppose need (iii) is replaced, before any licence is bought, by a requirement that the quarterly consolidation and the payroll system integration be performed automatically every period instead of producing a dashboard. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion about tool selection?
options: Power BI remains the appropriate tool, because the material says it aggregates and analyses data, and a consolidation is a form of aggregation.
ACL becomes the appropriate tool, because a consolidation performed without human effort is a data extraction exercise directed at irregularities.
CaseWare becomes the appropriate tool, because the material says it eliminates routine tasks and a periodical consolidation is routine.

Alteryx is the appropriate tool and the replaced need no longer engages Power BI, because the material names consolidations and system integrations among the set procedures performed periodically that Alteryx can automate.
No tool described in the material can meet the replaced need, because automation of periodic procedures is attributed only to macros and scripts.
questions.explanation: The decisive fact is that the replaced need is stated in the material's own vocabulary: Alteryx 'can also be used to automate set procedures that are performed periodically like reconciliations, consolidations, system integrations, continuous audits'. Power BI's described role is a platform for non-technical business users to aggregate, analyse, visualise and share data with such tools used for reporting through an interactive dashboard to higher management, so once the dashboard requirement disappears Power BI is no longer engaged. CaseWare's elimination of routine tasks is tied in the material to conducting audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently, not to executing consolidations or integrations, and ACL's description is confined to data extraction and analysis for fraud detection and prevention. The last option fails because macros and scripts appear in the range of automated solutions as rules-based automation, not as the only automation of periodic procedures.

Senior associate Neha proposes Power BI for need (i) because Power BI can aggregate and analyse data, and ACL for need (iv) because ACL is the best-known audit software in the industry.
Which of the following statements about the overlap between the four tool descriptions is/are CORRECT?
Statement 1: The material's descriptions of CaseWare and of Alteryx overlap, because CaseWare is said to eliminate routine tasks while Alteryx is said to automate set procedures performed periodically.
Statement 2: The material describes exactly one of the four tools as meant for non-technical business users.
Statement 3: The material attributes fraud detection and prevention to both ACL and CaseWare.
Statement 4: The material describes ACL as consolidating financial or operational data in order to assess controls.
options: Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the CaseWare entry says it 'helps in streamlining processes and eliminating the routine tasks' and the Alteryx entry says it 'can automate set procedures that are performed periodically', so the two descriptions genuinely overlap, which is why the case turns on which need is expressed in whose words. Statement 2 is correct: only the Power BI entry refers to non-technical business users. Statement 3 is incorrect because fraud detection and prevention appear only in the ACL entry, and Statement 4 is incorrect because consolidating financial or operational data to assess controls is the Alteryx description; attributing either to ACL is the common error of assuming that the most familiar audit brand carries every audit-related function. The option containing statements 3 and 4 is therefore wrong on both counts.

questions.question:
M/s Kulkarni & Associates, a thirty-partner firm, records four initiatives in its technology note for the year.
Initiative 1: an article clerk writes a small Visual Basic routine inside the audit spreadsheet that carries the client trial balance into the working papers by following a fixed set of rules; the design of the extraction process itself is left untouched.
Initiative 2: before any software is written, the firm maps its purchase-approval cycle, redrafts the process and removes two redundant sign-off stages, after which the redesigned process is implemented.
Initiative 3: a software bot is deployed to perform the identical repetitive activity of copying invoice data from the client portal into the audit file, an activity earlier done by a person.
Initiative 4: the bot of Initiative 3 is now combined with a system that can think and learn, so that it also decides which invoices deserve escalation.
In a review meeting a manager objects: 'Initiative 2 is not automation at all, so it cannot belong in a list of automated solutions; and Initiative 4 is merely a better bot, so its label remains the same as that of Initiative 3.'
Which of the following represents the correct matching of the initiatives with the labels used in the material's range of automated solutions?
Column I: A. Initiative 1 | B. Initiative 2 | C. Initiative 3 | D. Initiative 4
Column II: 1. Macros and Scripts - rules-based automation | 2. Business Process Automation - reengineering existing business process | 3. Robotic Process Automation - automating repetitive activities | 4. Intelligent Process Automation - combining RPA with AI
questions.explanation: The material lists the range of automated solutions as macros and scripts for rules-based automation, Business Process Automation for reengineering an existing business process, Robotic Process Automation for automating repetitive activities and Intelligent Process Automation for combining RPA with AI. Initiative 1 is a rules-based routine that leaves the process design untouched, so it is macros and scripts; Initiative 2 redesigns the purchase-approval process itself, which is BPA irrespective of whether software is written; Initiative 3 hands an identical repetitive activity to a bot, which is RPA; Initiative 4 adds a system that can think and learn to that bot, which is the material's definition of IPA. The first option fails because reengineering the process, not writing a rule, is what makes Initiative 2 BPA, and the fourth option fails by exchanging RPA and IPA even though the AI element is what distinguishes Initiative 4.

questions.question:
M/s Kulkarni & Associates, a thirty-partner firm, records four initiatives in its technology note for the year.
Initiative 1: an article clerk writes a small Visual Basic routine inside the audit spreadsheet that carries the client trial balance into the working papers by following a fixed set of rules; the design of the extraction process itself is left untouched.
Initiative 2: before any software is written, the firm maps its purchase-approval cycle, redrafts the process and removes two redundant sign-off stages, after which the redesigned process is implemented.
Initiative 3: a software bot is deployed to perform the identical repetitive activity of copying invoice data from the client portal into the audit file, an activity earlier done by a person.
Initiative 4: the bot of Initiative 3 is now combined with a system that can think and learn, so that it also decides which invoices deserve escalation.
In a review meeting a manager objects: 'Initiative 2 is not automation at all, so it cannot belong in a list of automated solutions; and Initiative 4 is merely a better bot, so its label remains the same as that of Initiative 3.'
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate evaluation of the manager's two objections?
options: Both objections are well founded, because the material's range of automated solutions covers only software that executes tasks.
The first objection is well founded but not the second, because reengineering a process is a management exercise while adding AI to a bot is a change of degree only.

Both objections are unsupported, because the material itself includes Business Process Automation, described as reengineering an existing business process, in the range of automated solutions, and gives a separate label, Intelligent Process Automation, to the combination of RPA with AI.
The second objection is well founded but not the first, because Initiative 3 and Initiative 4 both use a bot and the material recognises only one bot-based label.
Neither objection can be evaluated, because the material discusses process reengineering only in the context of cyber risk management.
questions.explanation: The material's range of automated solutions expressly includes Business Process Automation described as reengineering an existing business process, so a process redesign without any code is still inside the list and the first objection fails. The material separately names Intelligent Process Automation as the combination of RPA with AI, so the entry of a thinking and learning component changes the label rather than merely improving the bot, and the second objection also fails. The fourth option is the trap: it treats the word 'bot' as decisive when the decisive fact is the presence or absence of the AI component. The last option imports a context the material does not use for BPA.

questions.question:
M/s Kulkarni & Associates, a thirty-partner firm, records four initiatives in its technology note for the year.
Initiative 1: an article clerk writes a small Visual Basic routine inside the audit spreadsheet that carries the client trial balance into the working papers by following a fixed set of rules; the design of the extraction process itself is left untouched.
Initiative 2: before any software is written, the firm maps its purchase-approval cycle, redrafts the process and removes two redundant sign-off stages, after which the redesigned process is implemented.
Initiative 3: a software bot is deployed to perform the identical repetitive activity of copying invoice data from the client portal into the audit file, an activity earlier done by a person.
Initiative 4: the bot of Initiative 3 is now combined with a system that can think and learn, so that it also decides which invoices deserve escalation.
In a review meeting a manager objects: 'Initiative 2 is not automation at all, so it cannot belong in a list of automated solutions; and Initiative 4 is merely a better bot, so its label remains the same as that of Initiative 3.'
Suppose the vendor withdraws the thinking-and-learning component and Initiative 4 is completed using only the bot copying invoice data from the portal into the audit file. What changes, and which label now applies?
options: The initiative moves from IPA to RPA, because what remains is the automation of a repetitive activity and IPA exists only where RPA is combined with AI.
The initiative moves from IPA to macros and scripts, because once AI is removed what remains is rules-based automation.
Nothing changes, because the same activity was already automated before the learning component was added, and a bot remains a bot however reliable, fast or nonstop it is.
The initiative moves from IPA to BPA, because the removal of AI leaves a reengineered business process.
The initiative moves from IPA to continuous audit, because a bot copying data performs a periodic set procedure.
questions.explanation: The material defines Intelligent Process Automation as combining RPA with AI and Robotic Process Automation as automating repetitive activities; strip out the AI and the combination disappears, so the remaining initiative is a bot performing the identical repetitive copying activity, which is RPA. The second option is wrong because the residue is not a spreadsheet routine following fixed rules as in Initiative 1 - it is still a bot performing the activity a person used to perform. The third option ignores that the label itself is what changes, since the two entries are distinct items in the range. The fourth option wrongly treats the absence of AI as implying process reengineering, and the fifth imports Alteryx's list of periodically performed set procedures, which is a tool description and not one of the four labels.

questions.question:
M/s Ranganathan & Co audits Meridian Finance Ltd., a non-banking finance company. A single routine run on the complete loan and payment data of FY 2025-26 returns five outputs.
Output 1: 214 instances in which the same invoice number of the same vendor has been paid under two different payment references, aggregating ₹ 2.36 crore.
Output 2: 96 vendor accounts in which the payment released exceeds the amount due on the sanctioned purchase order, and 11 borrower accounts in which an overdraft has been allowed beyond the permitted limit.
Output 3: 1,100 ledger entries in which a credit balance is posted to an account coded as a debit-balance account and the posting date is later than the period end.
Output 4: a re-computation showing interest credited by the system at 8.5 per cent against the 9 per cent rate applicable under the criteria of the deposit scheme.
Output 5: 3,472 cash withdrawals each of more than ₹ 10,000.
The managing director asks that output 5 be switched off, arguing that ₹ 10,000 is only a tax threshold with no place in an audit routine, and asks the partner to explain what the software is doing that manual checking did not.
Which of the following classifies the outputs consistently with the examples of tests performed using CAATs given in the material?
options: 1 - Duplicate payments; 2 - Identify errors; 3 - Identify exceptions; 4 - Verify calculations; 5 - Accounts exceeding authorized limit
1 - Identify exceptions; 2 - Accounts exceeding authorized limit; 3 - Identify errors; 4 - Duplicate payments; 5 - Verify calculations
1 - Duplicate payments; 2 - Accounts exceeding authorized limit; 3 - Identify exceptions; 4 - Identify errors; 5 - Verify calculations
1 - Duplicate payments; 2 - Accounts exceeding authorized limit; 3 - Identify errors; 4 - Verify calculations; 5 - Identify exceptions
1 - Verify calculations; 2 - Accounts exceeding authorized limit; 3 - Identify errors; 4 - Verify calculations; 5 - Identify exceptions
questions.explanation: The material's five illustrative CAAT tests are identify exceptions (exceptional transactions, exemplified by cash transactions above ₹ 10,000), identify errors (inconsistent or erroneous data), verify calculations (re-performing computations, exemplified by the TDS rate applied as per criteria), duplicate payments (payment for the same invoice twice) and accounts exceeding authorized limit (payment beyond amount due or overdraft allowed beyond limit). Output 1 is the same invoice paid twice, so duplicate payments; output 2 states both limbs of the material's authorized-limit test; output 3 is internally inconsistent data, so identify errors; output 4 is a re-performance of a computation against applicable criteria, the same character as the TDS illustration; output 5 is the material's own exception illustration applied to the whole population. The third option is the tempting swap: it treats the credit-balance-with-future-date entries as exceptions, but the material's exception concept is the exceptional transaction, whereas wrong coding and impossible dates are erroneous data.

questions.question:
M/s Ranganathan & Co audits Meridian Finance Ltd., a non-banking finance company. A single routine run on the complete loan and payment data of FY 2025-26 returns five outputs.
Output 1: 214 instances in which the same invoice number of the same vendor has been paid under two different payment references, aggregating ₹ 2.36 crore.
Output 2: 96 vendor accounts in which the payment released exceeds the amount due on the sanctioned purchase order, and 11 borrower accounts in which an overdraft has been allowed beyond the permitted limit.
Output 3: 1,100 ledger entries in which a credit balance is posted to an account coded as a debit-balance account and the posting date is later than the period end.
Output 4: a re-computation showing interest credited by the system at 8.5 per cent against the 9 per cent rate applicable under the criteria of the deposit scheme.
Output 5: 3,472 cash withdrawals each of more than ₹ 10,000.
The managing director asks that output 5 be switched off, arguing that ₹ 10,000 is only a tax threshold with no place in an audit routine, and asks the partner to explain what the software is doing that manual checking did not.
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate response to the managing director's request to switch off output 5?
options: Switch it off, because an analytics routine should be configured only on limits arising from the entity's own accounting policy and materiality, and an amount lifted from tax legislation has no place in an audit exception report.

Decline, because the material's own illustration of the identify exceptions test is cash transactions above ₹ 10,000, so output 5 is an exceptional-transaction filter under the material and its retention is not made to depend on any tax provision.

Decline, because output 5 is the material's illustration of the duplicate payments test, cash withdrawals of the same round amount being payments made more than once, and duplicate payments cannot be detected at all once the filter is switched off, the list then having to be rebuilt voucher by voucher.
Switch it off and substitute a sample of cash vouchers, because the material treats sample auditing as the means of addressing exceptional transactions.
Decline, because output 5 evidences accounts exceeding authorized limit and the material requires such accounts to be reported to those charged with governance.
questions.explanation: The material lists 'identify exceptions: identify exceptional transactions, for e.g. cash transactions above ₹ 10,000' as an example of a test performed using CAATs, so the figure appears in the study material as an illustration of the exception test itself and the request rests on a mischaracterisation. The decisive fact is the identity of the test, not the legal source of the amount: output 5 flags transactions above a stated monetary criterion, which is what an exception report does. The third and fifth options misclassify output 5 as duplicate payments or as accounts exceeding authorized limit, both of which the material describes differently. The fourth option is wrong on two counts, since the material's description of auditing digitally moves from sample auditing to full population being reviewed and does not present sampling as the answer to exceptional transactions.

questions.question:
M/s Ranganathan & Co audits Meridian Finance Ltd., a non-banking finance company. A single routine run on the complete loan and payment data of FY 2025-26 returns five outputs.
Output 1: 214 instances in which the same invoice number of the same vendor has been paid under two different payment references, aggregating ₹ 2.36 crore.
Output 2: 96 vendor accounts in which the payment released exceeds the amount due on the sanctioned purchase order, and 11 borrower accounts in which an overdraft has been allowed beyond the permitted limit.
Output 3: 1,100 ledger entries in which a credit balance is posted to an account coded as a debit-balance account and the posting date is later than the period end.
Output 4: a re-computation showing interest credited by the system at 8.5 per cent against the 9 per cent rate applicable under the criteria of the deposit scheme.
Output 5: 3,472 cash withdrawals each of more than ₹ 10,000.
The managing director asks that output 5 be switched off, arguing that ₹ 10,000 is only a tax threshold with no place in an audit routine, and asks the partner to explain what the software is doing that manual checking did not.
Suppose the 96 vendor items are removed from output 2 by the client's explanation that each purchase order carried an escalation clause, leaving only the 11 borrower accounts where an overdraft was allowed beyond the permitted limit. What is the effect on the classification of the remaining items?
options: They become identify exceptions, because the payment limb of the authorized-limit test has disappeared.
They become duplicate payments, because an overdraft involves the same facility being used twice.
They remain accounts exceeding authorized limit, because the material describes that test as payment beyond amount due or overdraft allowed beyond limit.
They become identify errors, because an overdraft beyond the permitted limit is inconsistent data.
They become verify calculations, because a limit involves a computation.
questions.explanation: The material defines the test 'accounts exceeding authorized limit' with two alternatives - payment beyond amount due or overdraft allowed beyond limit - so either limb standing alone still answers to that description and removing the first limb does not move the second. The decision turns on reading the material's 'or' as two independent instances of the same test rather than cumulative conditions. The first option is the trap: the cash-withdrawal exception test in the material is about an exceptional transaction filter, not about a breached authorised limit. The second and fourth options misclassify a limit breach as data inconsistency or as repetition of the same invoice, neither of which describes an overdraft running past its permitted level.

questions.question:
M/s Ranganathan & Co audits Meridian Finance Ltd., a non-banking finance company. A single routine run on the complete loan and payment data of FY 2025-26 returns five outputs.
Output 1: 214 instances in which the same invoice number of the same vendor has been paid under two different payment references, aggregating ₹ 2.36 crore.
Output 2: 96 vendor accounts in which the payment released exceeds the amount due on the sanctioned purchase order, and 11 borrower accounts in which an overdraft has been allowed beyond the permitted limit.
Output 3: 1,100 ledger entries in which a credit balance is posted to an account coded as a debit-balance account and the posting date is later than the period end.
Output 4: a re-computation showing interest credited by the system at 8.5 per cent against the 9 per cent rate applicable under the criteria of the deposit scheme.
Output 5: 3,472 cash withdrawals each of more than ₹ 10,000.
The managing director asks that output 5 be switched off, arguing that ₹ 10,000 is only a tax threshold with no place in an audit routine, and asks the partner to explain what the software is doing that manual checking did not.
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
Statement 1: Output 4 is the material's verify calculations test, and re-computing an interest rate against the rate applicable under the scheme criteria is of the same character as the material's illustration of the TDS rate applied as per criteria.
Statement 2: Running the routine over the complete loan and payment data rather than a subset is consistent with the auditing digitally feature of improved quality of audit arising from full population being reviewed.
Statement 3: Output 3 is best classified as accounts exceeding authorized limit, because an account coded for a debit balance has been exceeded.
Statement 4: Outputs 1 and 5 concern payments and so the material treats them as the same test.
options: Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1 and 2 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the material's verify calculations test is the re-performance of computations and its illustration is the TDS rate applied as per criteria; re-performing an interest computation against the applicable criteria is the same operation on a different rate. Statement 2 is correct because the material links improved quality of audit under auditing digitally to moving from sample auditing to full population being reviewed, and the routine was run on the complete data. Statement 3 is incorrect: an account coded for a debit balance showing a credit balance, with a posting date after period end, is inconsistent or erroneous data, which is the identify errors test, and it has nothing to do with an authorised limit being exceeded. Statement 4 is incorrect because the material keeps duplicate payments for the same invoice and exception filters for exceptional transactions as separate illustrations, so any option admitting statement 3 or statement 4 is wrong.

questions.question:
The audit file of M/s Bhatia & Co for FY 2025-26 contains six observations recorded by the manager on review.
Observation 1: debtors' balancing is no longer tested through a sample of 60 balances; all 41,300 balances are reviewed.
Observation 2: extraction of data from the client's ERP, earlier done key-by-key by an article clerk, is now automated and transcription errors in the working papers have disappeared.
Observation 3: every journal entry posted after cut-off can be followed by the auditor from the initiating voucher through the ledgers to the financial statement line.
Observation 4: because technology has minimised the need for manual intervention, two team members were moved from routine ticking to areas requiring judgement.
Observation 5: the auditor now fixes the potential risk attaching to each significant account precisely, instead of flagging the whole cycle as high risk.
Observation 6: hours booked on the engagement fell by 18 per cent and the number of errors detected after the report date fell to nil.
Which of the following pairing of observation with the named key feature of auditing digitally is correct under the material?
options: Observation 1 - Improved efficiency; Observation 3 - Better risk assessment
Observation 3 - Increases transparency; Observation 5 - Better risk assessment
Observation 2 - Improved quality of audit; Observation 4 - Automation and ease
Observation 4 - Increases transparency; Observation 6 - Decreasing human dependency
Observation 5 - Improved quality of audit; Observation 1 - Better risk assessment
questions.explanation: The material states that transparency increases because technology traces the transaction end to end, which is exactly Observation 3, and that under better risk assessment the auditor may assess potential risk precisely, which is Observation 5. Observation 1 belongs to improved quality of audit, since the material ties that feature to moving from sample auditing to full population being reviewed, not to hours or error counts. Observation 2 is the material's own illustration of automation and ease, automating tasks like extracting data to reduce manual error, and Observation 4 is decreasing human dependency, technology minimising manual intervention. Observation 6 is improved efficiency, increased efficiency with fewer errors; pairing it with decreasing human dependency confuses the cause with the measured outcome.

questions.question:
The audit file of M/s Bhatia & Co for FY 2025-26 contains six observations recorded by the manager on review.
Observation 1: debtors' balancing is no longer tested through a sample of 60 balances; all 41,300 balances are reviewed.
Observation 2: extraction of data from the client's ERP, earlier done key-by-key by an article clerk, is now automated and transcription errors in the working papers have disappeared.
Observation 3: every journal entry posted after cut-off can be followed by the auditor from the initiating voucher through the ledgers to the financial statement line.
Observation 4: because technology has minimised the need for manual intervention, two team members were moved from routine ticking to areas requiring judgement.
Observation 5: the auditor now fixes the potential risk attaching to each significant account precisely, instead of flagging the whole cycle as high risk.
Observation 6: hours booked on the engagement fell by 18 per cent and the number of errors detected after the report date fell to nil.
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct as per the material's list of key features or advantages of auditing digitally?
Statement 1: Observation 6 evidences improved efficiency, expressed in the material as increased efficiency and fewer errors.
Statement 2: Observation 1 evidences improved quality of audit, expressed in the material as a move from sample auditing to full population being reviewed.
Statement 3: Observation 2 can only evidence decreasing human dependency, because the material confines automation and ease to tasks other than data extraction.
Statement 4: Observation 3 evidences better risk assessment, because tracing an entry tells the auditor where the risk lies.
options: Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: The question asks for the incorrect statements. Statement 3 is incorrect because the material's automation and ease feature uses data extraction as its express illustration - automating tasks like extracting data reduce manual error - so Observation 2 fits that feature as well as decreasing human dependency. Statement 4 is incorrect because end-to-end tracing of a transaction is the material's reason for the increases transparency feature, not for better risk assessment, which the material explains as the auditor assessing potential risk precisely. Statements 1 and 2 correctly reproduce the wording of two separate features, and options that include them fail on the polarity of the question.

questions.question:
The audit file of M/s Bhatia & Co for FY 2025-26 contains six observations recorded by the manager on review.
Observation 1: debtors' balancing is no longer tested through a sample of 60 balances; all 41,300 balances are reviewed.
Observation 2: extraction of data from the client's ERP, earlier done key-by-key by an article clerk, is now automated and transcription errors in the working papers have disappeared.
Observation 3: every journal entry posted after cut-off can be followed by the auditor from the initiating voucher through the ledgers to the financial statement line.
Observation 4: because technology has minimised the need for manual intervention, two team members were moved from routine ticking to areas requiring judgement.
Observation 5: the auditor now fixes the potential risk attaching to each significant account precisely, instead of flagging the whole cycle as high risk.
Observation 6: hours booked on the engagement fell by 18 per cent and the number of errors detected after the report date fell to nil.
The material describes auditing digitally as using technology advancements for conducting effective and efficient audit, and lists automation and ease and improved efficiency as two separate key features. Which of the following best shows, on these facts, that the material treats the two features as distinct?
options: Observation 2 concerns the reviewing of all balances, while Observation 6 concerns the tracing of entries.

Observation 6 alone evidences both features, because a fall in hours booked together with nil errors after the report date is simply the measurable consequence of having automated a task, and the material's automation and ease entry likewise turns on the reduction of manual error, so that one observation carries both labels.

Automation and ease is confined in the material to the extraction of data, so every observation about the disappearance of errors must be assigned to improved efficiency alone, the two entries being separated by subject matter rather than by outcome.

Observation 2 links the automation of a task, namely data extraction, to the reduction of manual error, which is the material's stated content of automation and ease, whereas Observation 6 reports increased efficiency with fewer errors, the stated content of improved efficiency.
The two features are not distinct, because the material's list of key features is also its list of advantages.
questions.explanation: The material assigns 'automating tasks like extracting data reduce manual error' to automation and ease, which is Observation 2, and assigns 'increased efficiency and fewer errors' to improved efficiency, which is Observation 6, so the two entries carry different stated content and the observations keep them apart. The first option misdescribes both observations. The second option collapses the two features into one observation, contrary to the material's separate entries. The third option applies the automation and ease feature too narrowly, treating it as excluding everything error-related when the material itself links it to the reduction of manual error. The fifth option confuses the fact that one list is headed 'key features or advantages' with the distinctness of the individual entries.

questions.question:
M/s Deshpande & Co attends a vendor demonstration and a partner immediately orders an analytics licence for all thirty audit teams, before any working paper identifies which audit procedures the tool will perform or which engagement problem it will solve. The IT cell is then told to become self-taught from vendor manuals, and the partner records in the note that the technology decision is complete because a recognised tool from the material's list has been bought.
Which of the following correctly identifies what the material's considerations require that is missing from this decision?
options: Only the requirement to upskill people, since the choice of tool necessarily settles the problem and the technology.
The requirement that the tool selected must review the full population rather than a sample, since that is the material's stated test of a technology decision.
The requirement that a general IT controls specialist be inducted into every engagement team before a licence is executed.
The requirement that continuous audit procedures be automated before any other procedure, since that is the first item in the material's list of tests.
The requirement to identify the problem the firm is trying to solve, the technology which can help, and how the people will be upskilled to make best use of the technology available.
questions.explanation: The material's considerations before adopting such technology are expressed as three questions: what problems are you trying to solve, which technology can help you, and how will you upskill your people to make best use of technology available. The firm has skipped the first and the third and has answered the second only by brand preference, so the note recording that the decision is complete is unsupported; the decisive fact is that buying a licence is not the same as identifying a problem. The option treating the choice of tool as automatically settling the problem inverts the material's order of thinking. The options insisting on full population review and on automating continuous audit first import material taken from other passages, namely the auditing digitally feature list and the Alteryx description, and the option demanding an IT controls specialist belongs to the separate discussion of control considerations, none of which forms part of the three considerations.

questions.question:
M/s Iyer & Associates builds an interactive dashboard for the audit committee of a listed client, the members of which are non-technical. The committee approves the dashboard as the means by which revenue findings will be shared with senior management. One director then asks why the dashboard should not itself be used to locate fictitious vendors, and the engagement team proposes to rely on the dashboard instead of running analytics over the payment data.
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate evaluation of the director's proposal?
options: Accept it, because the material says the platform provides non-technical business users with tools for aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data, and analysis of the payment trends so displayed is itself a means of detecting the irregularities which indicate fictitious vendors, so a separate run over the payment data would be duplicative.
Accept it, because the material says CaseWare shares analytical insights, and the dashboard in question is therefore a CaseWare output capable of the same function.

Reject it, because the material attributes fraud detection and prevention, and the finding of irregularities that indicate fraud in large data sets, to ACL Analytics, while the dashboard tool is described as serving non-technical business users in aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data for reporting.
Reject it, because the material confines interactive dashboards to internally generated management accounts and does not contemplate their use in an audit context.
Accept it only if the dashboard is rebuilt on Alteryx, because Alteryx is the tool described as assessing controls.
questions.explanation: The material's Power BI entry describes a platform giving non-technical business users tools for aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data, with such visualisation tools used for reporting in an interactive dashboard to higher management; that is a reporting and presentation role, and the dashboard is used to share findings already produced elsewhere. The locating of irregularities that indicate fraud in large data sets is expressly the ACL Analytics description, so substituting the dashboard for analytics over payment data replaces the tool the material associates with fraud detection with one it associates with presentation. The second option misattributes the dashboard to CaseWare, whose described functions concern conducting engagements quickly, accurately and consistently and eliminating routine tasks. The fourth option states a restriction the material does not impose, and the fifth confuses consolidation of data to assess controls with presentation of findings.

questions.question:
M/s Grewal & Co asks its analytics team to reduce the effort spent each quarter on four activities: (a) inter-unit consolidation, (b) reconciliation of branch collection accounts, (c) integrating the payroll extract into the ledger, and (d) running a continuous audit routine over monthly sales. The team leader records that the tool under discussion, Alteryx, supports automation of reconciliations only, because the material names consolidation and system integration for the purpose of assessing controls rather than as activities capable of being automated, and says continuous audit is an assurance approach and not an automatable procedure.
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
Statement 1: The team leader's exclusion of consolidation, system integration and continuous audit from automation is not supported, because the material lists reconciliations, consolidations, system integrations and continuous audits together as set procedures performed periodically that the tool can automate.
Statement 2: The material ascribes to Alteryx both the consolidation of financial or operational data to assess controls and the automation of set procedures performed periodically.
Statement 3: Activity (d) is one of the material's examples of tests performed using CAATs.
Statement 4: The material limits Alteryx's data consolidation to financial data and excludes operational data.
options: Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1 and 2 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the Alteryx entry ends with the words 'like reconciliations, consolidations, system integrations, continuous audits etc.', so all four activities fall inside the automation limb and the team leader's two grounds of exclusion fail. Statement 2 is correct because that entry carries two functions - consolidating financial or operational data to assess controls, and automating periodically performed set procedures. Statement 3 is incorrect because the material's examples of tests performed using CAATs are identify exceptions, identify errors, verify calculations, duplicate payments and accounts exceeding authorized limit, and continuous audit appears only in the Alteryx list. Statement 4 is incorrect because the entry expressly says financial or operational data.

questions.category: Data Analytics & CAATs - Meaning and Scope
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The material treats the use of Computer Assisted Auditing Techniques as increasing audit quality.
Reason (R): The material says CAATs involve the use of multiple data analytical tools or visualization tools that help the auditor to deep dive into the problem statement, and it is in that sense that audit quality increases.
Which of the following is the correct evaluation?
options: Both A and R are correct, and R is the explanation the material itself offers for A.
Both A and R are correct, but R explains the greater efficiencies mentioned by the material and not the increase in audit quality.
A is correct, but R is incorrect because the material attributes the increase in audit quality to full population review rather than to CAATs.
A is incorrect, because the material presents CAATs as a means of preparing information from raw data without any statement about audit quality.
A is incorrect but R is correct, because the material applies the expression deep dive to remote audit rather than to CAATs.
questions.explanation: The material's CAAT entry reads that data analytics methods used in audit are known as Computer Assisted Auditing Techniques, and that this involves use of multiple data analytical tools or visualization tools that help the auditor to deep dive into the problem statement and hence increase the audit quality. The word 'hence' makes the deep-dive the stated reason for the quality increase, so R is the explanation the material gives for A and the first option is correct. The second option is the strongest distractor: greater efficiencies and more accurate findings are attributed separately to the use of audit analytics, but that does not displace the express 'hence' linking deep dive to audit quality. The third option borrows the improved quality of audit wording from the auditing digitally features, where it is linked to full population being reviewed, and wrongly denies the CAAT statement. The fourth and fifth options contradict the text directly.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): One key feature or advantage of auditing digitally is stated in the material to be improved quality of audit, expressed as moving from sample auditing to the full population being reviewed.
Reason (R): The material describes ACL Analytics as sampling large data sets to find irregularities that indicate fraud.
Which of the following is the correct evaluation, taking the two passages exactly as the material states them?
options: Both A and R are correct statements of what the material says, and R is the reason for A.

Both A and R are correct statements of what the material says, but R does not explain A; the material does not reconcile the two passages and does not treat sampling as the general technique of CAATs.
A is correct but R is incorrect, because the material nowhere refers to sampling in describing any tool.
A is incorrect but R is correct, because the material's feature list refers to sample auditing without mentioning full population review.
Both A and R are incorrect, because the material describes CAATs as eliminating sampling altogether.
questions.explanation: A accurately reproduces the auditing digitally feature of improved quality of audit, which the material expresses as moving from sample auditing to full population being reviewed. R accurately reproduces the ACL Analytics entry, which says the tool samples large data sets to find irregularities that indicate fraud. The two passages therefore sit in visible tension and the material offers neither a reconciliation nor a general proposition that CAATs sample, so R cannot be the explanation of A and the second option is the only one that reports both passages faithfully. The first option quietly resolves the tension in one direction, while the third, fourth and fifth options each deny wording that is plainly present in the material.

questions.category: Data Analytics & CAATs - Meaning and Scope
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the material's use of terminology in the discussion of emerging technologies in audit.
Statement 1: The material uses the expression Data Analytics for generating and preparing meaningful information from raw system data using tools and techniques.
Statement 2: The material says that audit analytics or audit data analytics involves analyzing large sets of data to find actionable insights and trends, to draw conclusions and for informed decision making.
Statement 3: The material states that the use of audit analytics enables greater efficiencies and more accurate findings from the review process.
Statement 4: The material uses the expression Computer Assisted Auditing Techniques for data analytics methods that rely on a single standardized data analytical tool applied to a fixed problem statement.
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
options: Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 reproduce the material's three definitional moves: data analytics as generating and preparing meaningful information from raw system data using tools and techniques, audit analytics as the analysis of large data sets for actionable insights, trends, conclusions and informed decision making, and the consequence that audit analytics enables greater efficiencies and more accurate findings from the review process. Statement 4 is incorrect on two counts, because the material says CAATs involve the use of multiple data analytical tools or visualization tools and that they help the auditor deep dive into the problem statement, which is the opposite of a single standardized tool and a fixed problem statement. Note that the material speaks of raw system data, so a statement narrowed to summarised ledger balances would also be incorrect.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the key features or advantages of auditing digitally as listed in the material.
Statement 1: The feature of decreases transparency is expressed in the material as technology minimising manual intervention.
Statement 2: The feature of automation and ease is supported in the material by the illustration of automating tasks like extracting data, which reduce manual error.
Statement 3: The feature of better risk assessment is expressed as the auditor being able to assess potential risk precisely.
Statement 4: The feature of improved quality of audit is attributed in the material to increased efficiency and fewer errors.
Which of the following statements are NOT correct as per the material?
options: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because the material's transparency feature is expressed as technology tracing the transaction end to end, while minimising manual intervention is the content of decreasing human dependency; the statement also inverts the sign of the feature. Statement 4 is incorrect because increased efficiency and fewer errors is the material's separate improved efficiency feature, whereas improved quality of audit is attributed to the move from sample auditing to full population being reviewed. Statements 2 and 3 correctly reproduce their features, so any option including them fails on the polarity of the question. The recurring error tested here is the swapping of adjacent entries in the material's six-item list.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairings of an audit procedure with the category of test performed using CAATs, as the examples are set out in the material.
A. Extracting all cash payments of ₹ 45,000 made during the year and listing them for scrutiny - Identify exceptions.
B. Recomputing the TDS rate applied on professional fees against the rate due as per criteria - Verify calculations.
C. Listing vendor ledger entries where the same invoice number appears against two payment references - Duplicate payments.
D. Reporting customer accounts operating with an overdraft allowed beyond the permitted limit - Accounts exceeding authorized limit.
E. Reporting entries where text has been posted into a numeric ledger field - Verify calculations.
Which one of the above pairings is NOT correct as per the material?
options: A
B
C
E
D
questions.explanation: The material's verify calculations test is the re-performance of computations, illustrated by the TDS rate applied as per criteria, so pairing B is correct and pairing E is not: entries where data is inconsistent or erroneous fall under identify errors in the material, not under any computation. Pairing A is correct because the material's illustration of identify exceptions is cash transactions above ₹ 10,000, and a ₹ 45,000 cash payment is an exceptional transaction filtered out on a monetary criterion, the amount used being irrelevant to the category. Pairing C is the material's duplicate payment test, payment for the same invoice twice. Pairing D is the material's authorized-limit test, which expressly covers overdraft allowed beyond limit as well as payment beyond amount due.

questions.question: A firm's knowledge note describes auditing digitally using the following four statements. Which one of them is LEAST appropriate to the material?
options: It is described as the use of technology advancements for conducting an effective and efficient audit.
Its feature of increases transparency is supported by the material's statement that technology traces the transaction end to end.
It relieves the auditor of the task of assessing risk, because the technology itself performs the risk assessment.
It is linked in the material's feature list to increased efficiency together with fewer errors.
questions.explanation: The material's better risk assessment feature says that the auditor may assess potential risk precisely; the assessment therefore stays with the auditor and is only made sharper by technology, so the third statement is the least appropriate. The first statement reproduces the material's meaning of auditing digitally, and the second reproduces the wording of the transparency feature, tracing the transaction end to end. The fourth reproduces the improved efficiency entry, increased efficiency and fewer errors. The tempting reading behind the wrong option is that automation of procedures transfers judgement as well as effort, which the material's feature list does not support.

questions.question:
M/s Chokshi & Co records three proposals in its automation plan.
Proposal 1: a rules-based routine is written inside the audit spreadsheet to carry the client's sales register into the working papers; the existing process is followed as it is.
Proposal 2: the monthly analytical review is first redesigned, three duplicated approval steps being removed, and the redesigned process is then put into operation.
Proposal 3: a bot performing the repetitive copying of debtor balances is combined with a system that can think and learn, so that the bot also decides which balances to escalate.
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Proposal 3 corresponds to Intelligent Process Automation, described in the material as combining RPA with AI.
Statement 2: Proposal 1 corresponds to macros and scripts, described in the material as rules-based automation.
Statement 3: Proposal 2 corresponds to Business Process Automation, described in the material as reengineering an existing business process.
Statement 4: Proposal 1 evidences the auditing digitally feature of increases transparency, because a routine that copies data traces the transaction end to end.
Which of the above statements are CORRECT?
options: Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 to 3 each match a proposal to the label whose description the material gives: IPA as RPA combined with AI, macros and scripts as rules-based automation, and BPA as reengineering an existing business process. Statement 4 is incorrect because the material attaches increases transparency to technology tracing the transaction end to end, which is an audit trail property, whereas copying a register by fixed rules is at most the automation and ease illustration of automating the extraction of data. The options that omit statement 2 or statement 3 misread the labels, in particular the point that Proposal 2 contains no code at all yet is BPA because the process itself is redesigned.

questions.question:
For FY 2025-26 the analytics routine of M/s Sethi & Co reports cash transactions above ₹ 10,000 by processing the client's entire cash book for the whole year. For FY 2026-27 the partner raises the filter to cash transactions above ₹ 5,00,000 and, to save time, restricts the population to four months selected by the client's finance team.
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion under the material?
options: The filter remains the material's identify exceptions test, since it still isolates exceptional transactions on a monetary criterion; but restricting the work to four client-selected months departs from full population review, which the material gives as the source of improved quality of audit under auditing digitally.

The revised filter ceases to be a CAAT test, because the material fixes ₹ 10,000 as the exception criterion, so a filter set fifty times higher is no longer the test which the material illustrates, whatever population it is run on.

Both changes are unobjectionable, because the material's list of tests leaves the auditor free to set any monetary criterion and to work upon any population, the ₹ 10,000 figure and the whole-year run being illustrations of a test rather than conditions governing it, so neither change affects the audit approach, the population being tested or the conclusions drawn.

The revised filter becomes the duplicate payments test, because a threshold high enough to leave only a handful of items isolates payments of the same amount made more than once, which is what the material means by payment for the same invoice twice.

The revised filter remains a CAAT test only if it is run on ACL, because the material attaches the extraction of data and the finding of irregularities to that tool, so exception reporting is available through no other tool.
questions.explanation: The material's identify exceptions test is the isolation of exceptional transactions and its illustration is cash transactions above ₹ 10,000; the illustration fixes the kind of test, not the amount, so raising the threshold leaves the character of the test untouched. The second change does matter, because the material's improved quality of audit feature under auditing digitally is expressed as a move from sample auditing to full population being reviewed, and a four-month slice chosen by the client is a sample selected by the auditee. The second option therefore mistakes an example for a rule, the third treats the size of the population as a matter of free choice when the material's own feature list locates improved quality of audit in the full population being reviewed, the fourth confuses exception filtering with payment for the same invoice twice, and the fifth wrongly ties a test to a brand, the material listing tools and tests separately.

questions.question:
A partner of M/s Khanna & Co writes in a planning note: 'We need one tool that will consolidate the client's operational data so that we can assess its controls, and that will also carry out the monthly reconciliation and the continuous audit routine without repeat manual effort. CaseWare is the tool for this, because the material says it streamlines processes and eliminates the routine tasks.'
Which of the following is the MOST appropriate evaluation of this note?
options: The note is correct, because eliminating routine tasks is the same thing as performing a monthly reconciliation automatically, and a tool that streamlines processes necessarily executes the periodic procedures written into it.

The note is correct, because CaseWare is the only tool in the material described as providing tools that help in conducting audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently, and both a monthly reconciliation and a continuous audit routine are performed inside such an engagement, so its elimination of routine tasks covers precisely the work described in the note.

The note is incorrect, because the material attributes the consolidation of financial or operational data to assess controls, and the automation of periodically performed set procedures such as reconciliations and continuous audits, to Alteryx, while CaseWare's streamlining of processes and elimination of routine tasks is tied to the conduct of engagements.
The note is incorrect, because both functions described belong to Power BI, which the material says aggregates and analyses data.
The note cannot be evaluated, because the material does not describe any tool as consolidating operational data.
questions.explanation: The two requirements in the note are expressed in the material's Alteryx wording, both the consolidation of financial or operational data to assess controls and the automation of set procedures performed periodically like reconciliations and continuous audits. CaseWare's description is different in kind: tools that help in conducting audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently, sharing analytical insights for better informed decisions, and streamlining processes and eliminating routine tasks, which is engagement execution rather than consolidation of client data to assess controls. The first two options trade on the word 'routine', which appears in both descriptions but with different objects, and that overlap is precisely why the decisive fact is the stated purpose of consolidating data to assess controls. The fourth and fifth options misread the Power BI and Alteryx entries.

questions.question:
An article clerk, asked to check whether the client's payment master contains the same invoice paid twice, records in his note: 'This cannot be established by the analytics routine. Detection of duplication requires a person to compare payment vouchers, and in any event the population of 9 lakh payments must first be sampled.' A senior rejects the note without giving reasons.
Which of the following gives the correct basis, supported by the material, for rejecting the clerk's note?
options: The routine can perform the check, but only because the material says ACL samples large data sets, and 9 lakh payments is a large data set.

The routine can perform the check, because duplicate payment for the same invoice is listed by the material as an example of a test performed using CAATs, and the material's description of auditing digitally contemplates the full population being reviewed in place of sample auditing.

The note must be rejected because the material requires full population review in every audit, so the reference to sampling is wrong; whether CAATs can detect duplication is not addressed by the material.
The note must be rejected because Alteryx is described as automating continuous audits, and a duplicate payment check is a continuous audit.
The note is substantially correct, because the material attributes the finding of irregularities in large data sets to sampling by the tool.
questions.explanation: Two separate passages answer the clerk. The material lists duplicate payments, meaning payment for the same invoice twice, among the examples of tests performed using CAATs, so the check is one the routine performs over the data rather than a voucher-by-voucher human comparison. The material's key feature of auditing digitally is improved quality of audit arising from the full population being reviewed instead of sample auditing, so the premise that the 9 lakh payments must first be sampled is not supported. The first option picks up the ACL sampling sentence and treats it as the general rule for CAATs, which the material does not state; the fifth option compounds that error. The third option reaches the right result for the wrong half of the reason, since the material does address duplicate payment detection, and the fourth misclassifies the test.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements comparing two tool descriptions in the material.
Statement 1: The material describes the visualization platform as providing non-technical business users with tools for aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data.
Statement 2: The material describes CaseWare as sharing analytical insights which help in taking better informed decisions.
Statement 3: The material describes both tools as producing output presented to higher management through an interactive dashboard.
Statement 4: The material describes the first as a platform and CaseWare as data analysis software providing tools that help in conducting audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently.
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct?
options: Statements 1 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2 only
Statement 3 only
questions.explanation: The interactive dashboard for reporting to higher management appears only in the visualization platform entry, so statement 3 wrongly extends a distinctive feature of one tool to the other and is the single incorrect statement. Statements 1 and 4 reproduce that entry, which calls it a platform for non-technical business users aggregating, analysing, visualising and sharing data, and correctly contrast it with CaseWare as data analysis software providing tools to conduct audit and assurance engagements quickly, accurately and consistently. Statement 2 is correct: sharing analytical insights for better informed decisions is part of the CaseWare entry. The overlap in the word 'sharing' is what makes statement 3 attractive, but the objects shared, namely data on the one hand and analytical insights on the other, differ.

questions.question:
M/s Sabharwal & Co is appointed auditor of a supermarket chain with 3.2 crore point-of-sale transactions for the year. The partner sets three objectives before any tool is chosen: objective (a) revenue testing is to involve no sampling; objective (b) the monthly reconciliation between POS summaries and bank credits is to be performed automatically each period; objective (c) margin trends are to be shown to the non-technical functional heads through an interactive dashboard. A junior selects ACL for objective (b) and CaseWare for objective (c). No working paper records why these tools were chosen, and no training plan exists for the teams.
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Objective (a) evidences the auditing digitally feature of improved quality of audit, arising from full population being reviewed in place of sample auditing.
Statement 2: Objective (b) matches Alteryx's described automation of set procedures performed periodically, and the junior's selection of ACL for it is not supported by the material's description of ACL as data extraction and analysis software used for fraud detection and prevention.
Statement 3: Objective (c) is best served by CaseWare, because sharing analytical insights is the function the material attaches to it.
Statement 4: The absence of any record of the problem to be solved, the technology that can help and the upskilling of people leaves the material's considerations unaddressed.
Which of the above statements are CORRECT?
options: Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the material expresses improved quality of audit as a move from sample auditing to full population being reviewed, which is exactly objective (a) applied to 3.2 crore transactions. Statement 2 is correct because the material names reconciliations among the set procedures performed periodically that Alteryx can automate, while ACL's stated function is data extraction and analysis for fraud detection and prevention. Statement 3 is incorrect: the interactive dashboard for reporting to non-technical users and higher management is the visualization platform described in the material, and CaseWare's sharing of analytical insights is tied to conducting audit and assurance engagements and eliminating routine tasks, not to dashboard reporting. Statement 4 is correct because the material's considerations ask what problem is being solved, which technology can help and how people will be upskilled to make best use of the technology available, none of which is on the file.

questions.question:
While documenting technology risks arising from an entity's fully digital order-to-cash system, an auditor records the following four observations:
(1) The pricing program applies an incorrect discount formula, so it is processing data inaccurately.
(2) A former employee's access credentials to the customer database were never revoked, and he can still log in.
(3) The nightly database backup job silently failed for a fortnight, so data could not be restored when needed.
(4) A developer edited the live invoicing program without approval.
Using ONLY the eight example technology risks of digital systems listed in the source, which observation is mapped to the WRONG risk category?
options: Observation (1) - mapped to reliance on system/programs that are inaccurately processing data or processing inaccurate data
Observation (2) - mapped to inappropriate manual intervention
Observation (3) - mapped to potential data loss or inability to access data
Observation (4) - mapped to unauthorized changes to systems or programs
questions.explanation: The source's list contains 'unauthorized access to data' and 'inappropriate manual intervention' as two separate items. Observation (2) describes a live account that was never closed, which is unauthorized access to data, not manual intervention. Inappropriate manual intervention refers to a human circumventing or overriding an automated step in processing, which a stale credential is not. Observations (1), (3) and (4) are each mapped to a correct listed item, so only the mapping in option for observation (2) fails.

questions.question: Statement 1: Reliance on a system or program that is inaccurately processing data, or that is processing inaccurate data, is listed as a technology risk of digital systems. Statement 2: The source expresses the storage-related risk of digital systems as 'potential data loss or inability to access data'. Statement 3: The source expresses the change-related risk of digital systems as unauthorized changes to 'IT applications or other aspects of the IT environment'. Statement 4: The possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access is listed as a technology risk of digital systems. Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 reproduce the exact wording of the source's list of technology risks of digital systems. Statement 3 is incorrect because that list frames the change risk as unauthorized changes to 'systems or programs'; the wider phrase 'IT applications or other aspects of IT environment' is not the wording used in this list. The examinable point is the deliberate choice of vocabulary in the digital-systems list, which is narrower than a general IT-environment framing. Statements 1 and 2 also fix the two other wordings the list is particular about - the two-headed processing item and 'inability to access data'.

questions.question: During risk assessment of a digital inventory system, the auditor is told that no one ever deploys the quarterly security and functionality patches issued by the software vendor, so the programs remain as installed years ago. Which of the eight example technology risks of digital systems named in the source does this fact most directly evidence?
options: Failure to make changes to systems or programs
Inappropriate manual intervention
Unauthorized changes to systems or programs
Possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access
questions.explanation: The listed risk 'failure to make changes to systems or programs' captures exactly this situation, in which necessary updates simply are not made. It is not unauthorized change, because nothing was altered and no change was made without approval. It is not inappropriate manual intervention, which concerns a human overriding an automated process, and there is no question of IT personnel escalating their privileges. The decisive fact is the omission of required updates rather than a commission.

questions.question: An audit manager reviews a proposed response to the technology risk of a newly implemented cloud platform. The manager records: 'Engaging a cybersecurity control expert on the team is one of the key steps for evaluating the impact of a changing technology environment.' Is this characterisation correct, and why?
options: Correct - the source lists engaging a cybersecurity control expert on the team as one of the four key steps for evaluating the impact of a changing technology environment
Incorrect - considering whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary is a control consideration weighed while assessing technology risk, not one of the four key steps
Correct - the key steps and the control considerations are one and the same list in the source, so calling a specialist either a key step or a control consideration is acceptable
Incorrect - specialists such as cybersecurity control experts may be engaged only where the entity has actually suffered a cyber-attack during the period under audit
questions.explanation: The source places 'consider whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary (e.g. cybersecurity control experts, IT specialists in team)' inside the control considerations for assessing technology risk, not inside the four key steps. The four key steps are understanding the effects of new technology on risk assessment, maintaining professional skepticism, assessing management's control processes, and understanding the flow of transactions - none of them is 'engage a specialist'. The option claiming the two lists are identical ignores that the source keeps them as separate blocks; and the option permitting specialists only after a cyber-attack invents a precondition the source never states. The manager has therefore mislabelled a control consideration as a key step.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three control considerations that the source directs auditors to weigh while assessing technology risk?
options: Gaining a holistic understanding of changes in the industry and IT environment to evaluate management's process for initiating, processing and recording transactions
Considering risks resulting from implementation of new technologies and how those risks may differ from those arising from traditional systems
Considering whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary to determine the impact of new technologies and to assist in risk assessment
Understanding how technologies impact the flow of transactions and designing an appropriate audit response
questions.explanation: The three control considerations the source lists for assessing technology risk are a holistic understanding of industry and IT-environment changes, comparing new-technology risk with traditional-system risk, and considering whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary. The option about designing an appropriate audit response is not a control consideration - it is one of the four key steps for evaluating the impact of technology-driven changes. The test is placement: the source keeps the control considerations and the key steps as two separate blocks, and each distractor here is a genuine item from the block named in it.

questions.question: A team reviews management's risk assessment for a newly deployed automated revenue system and finds it unconvincingly favourable. Management asserts that the new self-correcting controls 'eliminate the risk entirely'. The auditor refuses to accept this assertion at face value and probes the basis of the conclusion. Which of the four key steps for evaluating the impact of technology-driven changes does this action best demonstrate?
options: Assess the appropriateness of management's processes to select, develop and maintain controls related to the organization's technology
Understand the effects of new technology and determine how it impacts the auditor's risk assessment
Maintain professional skepticism when reviewing management's risk assessment for new systems
Understand how technologies impact the flow of transactions and design an appropriate audit response
questions.explanation: The defining fact is the auditor's refusal to accept management's optimistic assurance about a new system, which is the professional-skepticism key step aimed squarely at management's risk assessment for new systems. The option about management's control processes is a different key step, directed at how controls are selected, developed and maintained rather than at the credibility of the risk assessment. The effects/risk-assessment option concerns the auditor's own understanding, and the flow-of-transactions option concerns response design. The decisive cue is scepticism directed at management's assessment of a new system.

questions.question: Before redesigning substantive procedures for an entity that replaced warehouse paperwork with a mobile-scanning application, an auditor works out how each sale now travels from scan to interface to general ledger, and then tailors his tests to that path. Which key step for evaluating the impact of technology-driven changes is being applied?
options: Maintain professional skepticism when reviewing management's risk assessment for new systems
Assess appropriateness of management's processes to select, develop and maintain controls
Gain a holistic understanding of changes in industry and IT environment
Understand how technologies impact flow of transactions and design appropriate audit response
questions.explanation: The auditor traces the route a transaction takes under the new technology and adapts procedures accordingly, which is precisely the flow-of-transactions key step. It is not the scepticism step, because management's assessment is not being challenged, and not the control-process step, because no evaluation of control selection or maintenance is described. The option about gaining a holistic understanding is mislabelled: that is a control consideration, not one of the four key steps. The decisive fact is the redesign of procedures around the transaction path.

questions.question: Statement 1: A control consideration directs the auditor to gain a holistic understanding of changes in the industry and IT environment to evaluate management's process for initiating, processing and recording transactions. Statement 2: A control consideration directs the auditor to consider risks resulting from implementation of new technologies and how those risks may differ from those arising from traditional systems. Statement 3: A control consideration directs the auditor to consider whether digital upskilling or specialists are necessary.
